name: main loop and global key handler
reason: Loop head runs the engine ping, module ping (0x402580), game-view redraw, flip and drains the message queue. Its key handler holds Escape/main menu, F7 quick save to the auto slot (refused for a dead PC or in another critter's turn-based turn, closes the world map first), F8 quick load, F10 compact toggle, the arrow scroll and the cheat keys (dead, cheat level is 0). Our nearest code is the viewer frame and input handling plus Arcanum.World.FrameStep, so no Arcanum.* method carries the key rules.

name: save file delete
reason: removes the project's snapshot, details and preview files; the auto slot is protected by its name whatever its description (the original protects only the file named with the Auto-Save description); a failed removal is reported where the original ignores it

name: latest save
reason: lists the project's snapshot files instead of gsi files; equal file times are ordered by name where the original's sort leaves them unordered

name: save list sort
reason: only the windows' order (auto slot first, then newest first, equal times by name); the name order the original uses for numbering is the new-save numbering of the save action

name: start-up logo movies
reason: Plays the Sierra and the Troika logo movies by fixed path (0x40DEE0), called from the game-module init 0x4020F0 (the game only, no condition). Steamwoven plays them before the first menu in the game build only (owner clarification 2026-11-12, ARC-RENDER-1242).

name: base archive mount
reason: Start-up mount of the base sources: lists the game folder's arcanum archives and mounts them, also takes archives that exist only in the registry install folder when the flag 0x5D0D70 is clear, then creates and mounts the data folder. Discover reproduces the base mount order (tig, game folder, arcanum archives by name, data) but reads only one game root and never creates folders; the registry fallback is left out.

name: module mount
reason: Module mount run at mod load: builds the module path (a bare name gets the modules folder prefix, a name starting with a backslash, a dot or a drive colon is used as given), mounts the module archive, up to ten patch archives and the module folder, with the registry install folder as a fallback; a failed module mount ends the load. Discover mirrors the module dat, patch 0..9 and folder order but refuses such path-like names, requires the dat for patches and has no install-folder fallback.

name: new prototype object
reason: Creates a prototype object of a given type: takes a pool slot, gives it a GUID later replaced by the prototype ID, a full value array sized for the type, clears every field and applies the type defaults (0x409000). Only the prototype builder uses it; our nearest code is Arcanum.Executable.Prototypes.PrototypeBuilder, which is not Data or World.

name: create object from prototype
reason: Creates an object from a prototype: copies only the type, the prototype link and the location, gets a GUID (a fresh one in the game, none in the editor), registers it in the find index and for a critter or trap-like type writes the day and night standpoints and a flag; the presence bitmap starts empty so all else reads through the prototype. We have no generic create-from-prototype method, only per-kind session creation such as projectiles and missiles.

name: create object with given id
reason: Second front door of object creation: runs the creator 0x4058E0, then replaces the new GUID with the requested ID, removing the old registry entry and registering the requested one. Used by the creation with an ID (0x442130); no counterpart in our code.

name: free object
reason: Frees an object's storage: removes it from the find index, drops its registry entry (a no-op in the retail build), releases its value and array fields and the presence bitmaps; the ID then resolves to nothing. Our records are managed; the object removal rules of the session stores are the nearest, with no method carrying this.

name: free temporary object
reason: The release half of free object (0x405BF0) without the find index step: clears a prototype's or instance's fields and arrays, then the registry entry; it frees the temporary copy that 0x405D60 made for the auto-level preview (0x4A6E40). No counterpart in our code.

name: temporary object copy
reason: Makes a scratch copy of an object (type, ID, prototype link, location, value arrays and presence bitmaps, then reapplies the inventory via 0x464470) used by the auto-level rule to try a scheme on a copy. Our auto-level code works on records without a clone of this kind.

name: duplicate object
reason: Duplicates an object: copies the type, prototype link, presence bitmap, own values and location, assigns a new GUID, and for a container or critter walks the inventory list and duplicates each item recursively into the copy. Reached from the copy creators 0x4421A0; the per-item step is an inference from the call shape. No counterpart in our code.

name: duplicate object with given id
reason: Duplicate object with a requested ID: runs 0x406010, then replaces the new GUID with the given ID and re-registers it, and re-registers each duplicated inventory item with a given ID as well. Used by the copy with an ID (0x4421A0); no counterpart in our code.

name: object id get
reason: Returns the 24-byte ID of an object: a stale handle gives the registry reverse-lookup ID or null; an object that has none yet gets one on first request, a positional ID (location, temporary ID field 328, map) for a static wall, portal, scenery or trap in the game and otherwise a GUID, is added to the registry and marked as having a new ID; an invalid ID is logged. Our nearest are the session object records keyed by map+entity or oid, with no lazy identity assignment.

name: object field value write
reason: The core field writer: finds or creates the instance own slot even when the value equals the prototype value, copies the value in by the field storage kind (32-bit, 64-bit, 24-byte ID, array), sets the presence bit and the object modified mark (the transient fields 315 to 333 are written inline without the mark). Ours has no sparse own-slot storage; the session records changes per feature.

name: object array element write
reason: The core array element writer: finds or creates the instance own array slot (copying the prototype array first when needed), writes the element by the element storage kind and sets the presence bit and the object modified mark. Ours has no such storage; changes are kept as per-feature session records.

name: object field value read with prototype fallback
reason: The core field reader: returns the instance own value when its presence bit is set and otherwise the prototype value found through the cached prototype handle (0x40D630); transient fields 315 to 333 are read inline and field 335 returns the type directly. Ours reads immutable base records of the loaded map with no read-time prototype fallback (plan SP1).

name: array field element getter
reason: Reads one element of an array field (script, quest, integer or handle arrays; kinds 5 to 13) into the caller record, with a prototype and instance rule: a prototype reads its own slot, a transient field (315 to 333) is read inline, an instance that owns the field reads its own array, otherwise the whole array of its prototype is used (no per-element fallback). The element is copied out by the field kind width and an absent slot reads as zeros. Ours has no generic getter; the nearest code is the per-field reads of CombatFieldReader.Read and the map-row model, which do not model the prototype fallback as one rule.

name: array field length getter
reason: Returns the number of elements of an array field with the same own-or-prototype rule as the element getter 0x408BB0: a prototype reads its own slot, an instance that owns the field its own array, otherwise the prototype handle is resolved and its array counted (via the array store 0x4E4BA0). Only caller is the field length accessor 0x4079C0. Ours has no generic length getter; the nearest is CombatFieldReader.Read where script and effect lists are read from the record or the prototype.

name: array field element write preparation
reason: Write path for array fields: a prototype writes its own slot; a transient field is written inline; for an instance that does not yet own the field it first creates the instance own copy of the prototype array (marking the field present and the object modified), then stores the element through the array store 0x4E4B70. Ours keeps mutable object state as project keys over immutable map rows (OM9, OM10), so there is no copy-on-first-write of a prototype array; nearest is Arcanum.Session object-field state, not an equivalent.

name: field slot address resolver
reason: Resolves where a field value lives: a prototype uses its own slot, a transient field (315 to 333) the inline cell, an instance that owns the field its own slot, otherwise the slot of the prototype found through the prototype handle (0x40D630). Returns the pointer used by the array and typed accessors; no write or presence change. Ours has no pointer-level resolver; field inheritance is applied field by field (nearest: Arcanum.Data.Combat.CombatFieldReader.Read).

name: prototype file record reader
reason: Reads a prototype record from the file: version-checked by the dispatcher 0x406600, then the blocked ID, the own ID, the object type and the whole array of the type fields (callback 0x40A140), after which the object is registered with its transient state cleared. Ours reads the same layout with prototype=true and rejects a prototype whose IDs are not the blocked/own pair; the in-memory registration, handle allocation and transient fields are left out because our records are immutable rows.

name: instance file record reader
reason: Reads an object record from the file: IDs, type, field count, presence mask words, then the fields whose bits are set (callback 0x40A290); afterwards it sets the loaded flag (field 332) on the object and registers its GUID/ID in the registry. Ours reads the same layout and checks that the mask population equals the count; the registration, the loaded flag and the instance own-slot construction are left out (immutable map rows).

name: single handle to id conversion
reason: Converts each single-handle field the object owns into an ID before a save or move: a stale handle takes the ID the registry last had, a target destroyed and not extinct becomes a null ID, an extinct (teleported) target keeps its ID. Ours links objects by identity with no handle layer, so this null-on-destroyed rule has no counterpart method.

name: handle array to id conversion
reason: Walks the handle-array fields of an object (inventory lists, follower lists and the like) and converts each element through the per-element callback 0x40BF00, logging a failed array; the null-element-in-place rule for destroyed targets has no counterpart in our code, which saves references by identity.

name: single id to handle conversion
reason: After a load or arrival, turns each single-handle field that holds an ID into the registry handle, or null when the ID is not found; a link to an object of another map thus becomes null. We resolve references by identity and have no handle step, so there is no matching method.

name: handle array id to handle conversion
reason: Walks the handle-array fields and converts every element ID to a registry handle through the callback 0x40BFC0, keeping a null element in place on a miss and logging a failed array; no counterpart in our identity-based references.

name: array element handle to id callback
reason: Per-element step of 0x40BD20: a null element stays; an element not in the registry is turned into the last known ID; a live target keeps its ID; a destroyed and not extinct target becomes null in place. Nothing of ours does this null-on-destroyed conversion.

name: create default player character at start
reason: Original: looks up the object of prototype 15, takes the start location stored in the current map's list entry (a computed fallback when it is zero), creates the object there, makes its art ids and stores it as the player global; called from the new-game reset 0x4B9BE0. Ours: builds the owner from bootstrap rules and creates no default hero that character creation later replaces (documented difference, PS6).

name: player object creation
reason: Makes a new player character: picks the prototype (generic player type or the given number), takes the id and location from the request or from the old player, destroys the old player, creates the object, stores field 0xF2 and the current map number in field 0xF3, makes it the local player, generates the prototype inventory (0x463E20) and clears the inventory source field 0xEF. Our nearest code is the pre-made hero reader AreaStartingHero.Load and the session hero build, which build the hero from a definition and do not replay this create/destroy sequence.

name: play movie by number
reason: The lookup of the number in the module movie table (movies\movies.mes) and the path of its file in the content stack (a loose file, or an archive member copied once to a cache folder); a number with no row, 0 and a name that is not a plain .bik name plays nothing. Playing and the sound lock are the viewer's (TerrainViewerApp.PlayMovies, ARC-RENDER-1170). Callers: View Intro (1 and 7) and the new game's start (1 and 7) play; start-up (movie 8) is not played (owner decision 2026-11-12); script action 103 and the teleport's own movie numbers are not admitted yet.

name: play movie by path
reason: Resolves the path (0x52F410), locks the sound system (0x41C610), maps the caller flags to the player flags, plays through 0x531530 and unlocks (0x41C660); a path that does not resolve plays nothing and does not lock. Steamwoven: the viewer resolves the path (AreaMovieTable.PathOf), stops the scene and menu sounds for the movie instead of the session's lock state, and plays through the player ffmpeg decodes (TerrainViewerApp.PlayMovies, ARC-RENDER-1170); no counted method.

name: view scroll step
reason: The scroll function: passes at most once per the fps interval, then for a direction code 0-7 takes the step from the speed table (diagonals 4 and 2 pixels larger), applies the distance limit around the local player (box of 80 and 40 pixels per tile of the Perception-based distance, steps toward the player free, blocked or axis-trimmed steps otherwise), picks the scroll or blocked cursor (0x2A6 plus the code) and passes the pixel offset to the apply function 0x40E630. Ours has the step, the limit and the blocked answer (OriginalScroll.Limit) and the rate gate (OriginalScrollClock.TryStep); left out are the cursor choice, the pointer warp, the override callback (0x5D11C8) and the applying of the offset, which the viewer does.

name: scroll distance limit
reason: Answers zero (no limit) when the distance switch is off or there is no player, else the local player Perception halved towards zero plus three tiles. Ours takes the Perception as an argument and leaves the switch and the no-player test to its caller (a distance of 0 means no limit).

name: scroll speed table
reason: Sets the across and up/down pixel steps from the speed level: 8/4, 20/10, 28/14 or 56/28; with an override mode set it derives them from the override value in four other ways. Ours has the four-level table (HorizontalStep and VerticalStep) and the level the game always runs at, not the override branch, which nothing can reach.

name: map open
reason: Opens a map from its module folder and the save folder in a fixed order: close the old map, check the folder, read map.prp (required) and startloc.txt, load the initial mobile objects from the module cache, apply mobile.md, mobile.des and Rules map.patch, read mobile.mdy, convert ids to handles and queue Teleported events, then terrain, jump points, blocked sectors, start location and map id, mapinfo.txt, off-flags outside the sector limits and the gender log check. Our nearest code reads the same module files (WorldCatalog.Open, ReadMobiles, ReadTerrain, AreaWholeMobile) but does not reproduce the open order or the post-load steps as one operation; the sector cache itself is lazy as in the original.

name: map open in game
reason: Opens a map by its list number for play: rejects a number outside 1..count, flushes the current map first when asked, runs the object pass 0x405280, builds the module and save folder paths, opens the map with the keep flag (0x40F4E0), stores the map start location as the current location, moves the view (0x4B8CE0), optionally pre-caches 3 by 3 sectors and runs 0x45C580 and 0x4605C0 and the pass again. Our change of place (Arcanum.Session change-of-place movers and AreaChangeOfPlace) does the visible parts but not this sequence as one function.

name: sector pre-cache 3 by 3
reason: Locks and unlocks the nine sectors around a location (wrapping the coordinates in 26 bits) so they stay loaded in the cache. Ours touches one cell of each sector around the hero cell after an arrival and skips negative sectors; it takes no arbitrary location and does not lock and unlock.

name: map start location get
reason: Gives the start location of a map-list row as two 64-bit values (x and y), or zeros and failure for a number outside 1..count. Ours holds it as the property MapListEntry.Start (null when the row has fewer than three values or a negative coordinate), not as a method.

name: map world-map number get
reason: Gives the WorldMap value of a map-list row (minus one outside 1..count); only the world-map window caller 0x560AA0 reads it. Our map list loader skips the WorldMap value.

name: jump point at tile
reason: For a tile the player entered, finds the first jump point there (0x4E3450, flags not checked) and, while fewer than nine jump teleports are nested, asks for a teleport to its destination map and cell (0x4D3380) with flags 0. Ours queues the first jump point site of the cell before the tile script and drops it when a transfer is already pending; the nesting counter of nine is not modelled.

name: map open post-load fix-up of objects
reason: For every non-static object turns its saved IDs back into handles, then for each object holding the teleported flag (0x40000000 of field 0x13) queues a Teleported event 1 ms ahead (0x45B820, type 32) and clears the flag. Ours takes the mark off every object of the opening map in one revision and returns the objects to notify; the ID rebinding does not exist in our model and the event itself is scheduled by the viewer, not by this method.

name: map extension file read
reason: Reads the map's mapinfo.txt line by line (key before the colon, case-insensitive): LightScheme sets the map default scheme when positive and applies it for the current hour, SoundScheme takes two comma-separated numbers and, when sound is on, sets the music and ambient scheme through 0x41BD50; other keys are ignored and a later line wins. Our reader only parses the file into the map info record (the application happens in the lighting and audio code), and treats a bad value as an issue instead of silently reading 0.

name: map patch token reader
reason: Skips C white space, then copies the run of non-white characters into the caller's buffer and advances the cursor, answering 0 at the end of text (isspace through the locale table or the CRT call depending on the code page). Ours splits on ASCII white space and returns null at the end; the original's unbounded copy and non-ASCII locale classification are not reproduced.

name: apply one map patch line to an object
reason: Applies the attribute text after the line's first colon to the found object: keys compare ignoring case, values are the next token (atoi, stand points 64-bit), and it writes internal and known name, alignment stat (clamped, followers re-check), origin, notify_npc, magic hit adjust, obj, portal, item, critter and npc flag names (a leading ! clears the bit), training, script slot header, day and night stands, magic and tech complexity, level scheme and faction; a field the object's type lacks is not written and an unknown key stops the line. Ours does not model training (tier steps gated by skill level), the alignment side effects, or the crash on a matched line without a colon.

name: map list load
reason: only the rows, their numbering, (ARC-UI-038) their type and (ARC-SCRIPT-050) their area (the other map properties are read by the map catalogue); a long name is accepted and the name trimmed, a row with fewer than three values keeps no start where the original crashes, a negative start is dropped and an overflowing coordinate saturates where the original wraps (IF2)

name: map list find by name
reason: Scans the map list table for the first entry whose name matches case-insensitively and returns its index or -1; ours returns the entry and folds case with the ordinal ignore-case comparison, which also folds non-ASCII letters where the original uses the ASCII-fold string compare (with a locale branch)

name: dialog file load
reason: Opens the DLG of a script through the dialog cache: a cached name only gains a reference and a fresh time stamp, otherwise a slot is filled by the record reader (0x417720) and the load is refused when no record was read. Ours reads the winning copy at every call and refuses an empty document the same way; the cache, its reference counts and time stamps are not built.

name: dialog start
reason: Starts a talk: refuses when the NPC cannot speak to the PC (can-speak 0x4AD800), opens the reaction conversation slot (0x4C1020), answers a living kill-on-sight NPC with a race line (0x4185F0 base 1000) and the ended state 4, turns the view toward the pair for the local player, then enters the node and builds the reply list (0x414E60). Ours opens the reaction slot before the first NPC line and runs the node; the can-speak refusal, the hostile start and the view step are not built.

name: dialogue reply step
reason: only the hostile check after the action string (alive and kill-on-sight toward the PC through the hostility port: the NPC speaks a generated line that is not loaded and the talk ends; a string with FL, JO, UW, ET or SU returns 0 and is not checked, HR1–HR3); the can-speak refusal of the pick, the stored response (state 3) and the same check at the dialog start are not built; the transition switch (0x414810) is the conversation runtime's own

name: dialog end
reason: Only calls the conversation end (0x4C10A0) with the PC and the NPC, which moves the slot-0 reaction value to the PC remembered slot. Ours closes the reaction slot the host opened through the session on every exit path of a talk.

name: generic greeting text
reason: only the text: the host floats it over the NPC (no window) through its script float line, the log record and the speech of the original's display 0x568540 are not made (GT223); the slot text is passed for a follower only; the can-speak refusal is not made; the NPC and the PC facts are the host's (as 0x419260)

name: leave farewell line
reason: only the range by reaction level (the D3 setting may swap it); the can-speak test, the line file by both genders and the random line are the host's

name: speak dialog node with can-speak gate
reason: Speaks one node: with the flag clear it first asks the can-speak test and, when refused, clears the line and the stored response index; otherwise it stores the node, sets state 0 and runs the NPC line step (0x416840). Ours enters nodes in DialogConversation (Enter, Greet) without the can-speak refusal.

name: follower leave refusal line
reason: After the can-speak test (flag 1) it picks the NPC line range of the refusal reason through a seven-entry table: too good 1600, too evil 1700, dislike 1800, already grouped 2600, limit 2700, not allowed 2800, low level 2900 (100 lines each), then picks a line (0x418780). Ours holds the range table only; the can-speak test, the line pick and the float are the host.

name: follower acknowledgement line
reason: After the can-speak test (flag 1) it picks a random NPC line 2100-2199 (the order acknowledgement); called by the follower orders (broadcast 0x4C31A0) and by the dialog actions ce, ii and ri, which set a pending window code. Ours holds the range of the acknowledgement line for the orders; the pick, the float and the dialog actions are not built.

name: follower cannot do line
reason: After the can-speak test (flag 1) it picks a random NPC line 2200-2299 (the follower cannot do the order) for the order handlers (0x4C31A0). Ours holds the range only; the pick and the float are the host.

name: curse race insult line
reason: After the can-speak test it picks a race insult line from base 1000 of the race line tables (0x4185F0) for a follower that left after a curse order. Ours leaves the line to the host (the session orders only name the insult).

name: follower line on attack event
reason: After the can-speak test it picks a random NPC line 2300-2399, floated by the attack event handler (0x4A9650) for a follower after a roll and an activity test. No counterpart is built.

name: surrendered npc line
reason: After the can-speak test it picks a random NPC line 3000-3099 (override record 12029) for a surrendered NPC; called by the greeting builder and by two AI paths (0x4AA620, 0x4AABE0). Ours says it only inside the greeting (DialogGreeting.NpcLine); the two AI callers are not built.

name: follower taunt line
reason: After the can-speak test it picks the NPC line range of the taunt kind: kind 0 (critical hit) 2400-2499, kind 1 (stray hit) 2500-2599. Ours holds the range per kind; the pick and the float are the host.

name: guard crime notice line
reason: After the can-speak test it picks a random NPC line 4000-4099, called by the guard notice of a portal or container crime (0x4AEE50). No counterpart is built.

name: newspaper headline intro line
reason: After the can-speak test it picks a random NPC line 4100-4199, called by the float-headline script action (0x4494DF, action 86, after punctuation is appended) before the headline is floated. Our script dispatcher has no counterpart.

name: follower leader warning line
reason: After the can-speak test (flag 1) it picks the NPC line range of the leader warning: too good 5200, too evil 5300, low reaction 5400 (100 lines each); any other value yields no line. Ours holds the range table only; the pick and the float are the host.

name: upset line
reason: the message range by reason; the can-speak test and the line text are the host's

name: follower near death line
reason: After the can-speak test it picks a random NPC line 5500-5599 floated toward the PC leader when a follower falls below one fifth of its hit points. Ours holds the range as the property FollowerRules.NearDeathLines (not a method) and leaves the pick to the host.

name: dialog reply state dispatch
reason: Switch over the 31 reply states that follow a picked reply: direct node entry (state 0), end, barter, money offer and payment, skill and rumor offers, healer, teacher and the other generated services, each calling its own builder. Ours handles the direct, end, script-line, join, final line, expert teacher, schematic, sheet, identify, repair and barter transitions in Select; the money request, healer, skill, rumor and training states are not built.

name: dialogue reply list
reason: only the phrase of the no-reply farewell (PC lines 400..499) and the phrases picked in offer order; a rebuild keeps the turn's phrases instead of reseeding the generator with the saved seed, and the reply gates and the five-reply cap follow the conversation runtime's reading

name: dialog reply eligibility scan
reason: Looks up the NPC entry and walks its reply rows in order, keeping up to five whose gender matches the PC (or is -1), whose IQ gate holds against the effective IQ (a dumb PC counts 1) and whose condition string passes the condition interpreter (0x4150D0). Ours does the same per reply in BuildOffers and IsEligible; the stored seed and the sorted-table lookup are not reproduced.

name: dialogue condition
reason: only the ME branch (0 not met, 1 met; the original passes any other operand without a test, where the conversation stops at an unsupported-operation frontier), the RP branch (n > 0 holds n, n ≤ 0 lacks −n; ARC-WORLD-044) the GV, PV and PF branches (the cell equals the second operand, ARC-DEV-152, DG1–DG2), the QU, QA and QB branches (cases 8, 24 and 21: the PC's quest state against the second operand with signed compares, equal, at least, at most; ARC-DEV-180, DCC4, QL1; ReadQuest) and the `$$` branch (case 10: the signed rule on the gold of the PC and its direct followers, a 32-bit wrapping sum, ARC-DEV-179, DCC5, GM1; ReadGold); the SS, AR and IA branches (cases 27, 33 and 35: the signed rule on the story state, the PC's area known (n > 0) or not known (n ≤ 0), the PC's map area equal (n > 0) or different (n ≤ 0); ARC-DEV-191, DCC7, SV1, SV3–SV4, F1; ReadWorldFact), the CH, PE, LE, AL, MA, TA and NA branches (cases 1, 2, 20, 3, 4, 5 and 32: the signed rule on the PC's charisma, perception, level, alignment and aptitude, TA on the negated aptitude, NA the alignment against the negated operand, from the stat getter's values; ARC-DEV-192, DCC2–DCC3, PQ1–PQ5, F1; ReadStat), the IN and NI branches (cases 11 and 23: the PC or a follower holds an item by name for a non-negative operand, the NPC or its substitute container for a negative one, NI the exact negation; ARC-DEV-194, DCC6, IH1–IH4, F1; ReadItem), the FO and WT branches (cases 19 and 29: the NPC's leader is the PC, also while it waits; its jilted flag is set; operand 1 asks for it, 0 for the opposite; ARC-DEV-195, DCC8, CF1, F1; ReadCompanion), the LC branch (case 14: the NPC's dialog-point attachment counter i, a byte of the counter word at 8·i modulo 32 bits, equals the second operand; the index wraps modulo 4 and a missing second operand reads 0; ARC-DEV-196, ARC-DEV-228, DCC9, KC1, F1; ReadCounter), the PA branch (case 26: a direct follower of the PC, not mind-controlled, whose name field equals the operand's magnitude, none for a negative operand; ARC-DEV-227, DCC8, PN1, F1; ReadFollower), the SC branch (case 36: the PC's rank in college n from the getter 0x4B1AB0 against v: above 0 at least v, otherwise at most -v; ARC-DEV-197, DCC10, CK1, F1; ReadCollege), the other admitted operations follow the conversation runtime's reading and are not checked here

name: dialogue action
reason: only the RP branch (n > 0 adds n, n ≤ 0 removes −n), the GV, PV and PF branches (the cell takes the second operand, a PF value only 0 or 1 in the subset; ARC-DEV-152, DG3–DG4), the `$$` case (case 0, ARC-DEV-179, DAC2, GM2–GM4: n > 0 gives the PC coins from nothing; n < 0 the PC pays and the followers pay what is left, the Original setting with the bug that a payer holding less than the amount owed pays nothing yet lowers it by all it holds, SessionDialogGoldPort), the XP case (ARC-DEV-178, DAC9: the PC gets the experience of quest experience level n, a level without a table entry gives nothing) and the SU case (ARC-TECHNOLOGY-006, NC1: the schematic window with the NPC as crafter and the PC as viewer, the operand ignored, the rest of the field run and the reply's target node skipped; SU with JO, UW, FL, ET or an insult in the same reply and SU in an NPC line's own action, F1, are outside the subset) and the CO case (case 4: a flag only, the attack event of the PC on the NPC at loudness 1 with no flags after the whole string, a final line in the string first, only a `co` kept behind an `fl`; ARC-DEV-190, CA1–CA2, F1; the hostile re-check of the reply step after the string is not modelled, CA3); the SS case (case 18: the story state setter, which keeps the larger value; ARC-DEV-191, DAC7, SV2, F1); the IN case (case 9, the operand not negative: the first hero item named n, kit then taken then made, goes to the NPC through the session's move; nobody holding it does nothing; a follower-only item is refused; name: dialogue npc line
reason: only the g: greeting branch after the node's actions (ARC-WORLD-058); the i:, m: and r: markers stay frontiers and a node without a marker follows the conversation runtime's reading

name: dialog entry lookup by number
reason: Binary search of the dialog slot records for one entry number, copying the 28-byte entry out; false when absent. Ours keeps a dictionary by number and takes the first record of a duplicated number; the original sorts with an unstable qsort and its search may land on either duplicate.

name: dialogue name substitution

name: dialogue option builder

name: dialog record loop
reason: Opens the file, reads entries with the entry parse (0x417860) until it stops, growing the record array by ten, then sorts the records by number (qsort with the 0x417E00 comparator). Ours runs the same record loop and stop rules; the records stay in file order with a by-number dictionary instead of a sort.

name: dialogue entry copy

name: number list expand

name: generated dialog file open

name: generated pc line

name: generated pc class line

name: story state player phrase
reason: Builds the PC phrase of the m: reply marker: one PC line numbered 1700 plus the story state (0x445090) through the PC line builder (0x4182D0). Ours has no m: marker phrase (DialogGreeting.Phrase does not offer it).

name: generated class line

name: generated race line

name: generated npc line
reason: as the class line

name: greeting override line

name: dialog money request
reason: Starts a money request in a talk: the price is the reaction-scaled amount (0x4C1150) with 1 raised to 2, the NPC says a class line (group 1000) with the price formatted into it, and two PC options are built (pay, refuse, PC lines 1-99 and 100-199) with state 2 and price kept for the pay step. Ours has the price scale (TradeRules) but no money request in the dialog.

name: dialog pay request
reason: Pay step of a money offer: when the PC holds at least the price (0x464780) it takes the coins (0x464830, PC to NPC, an optional log record) and continues with the stored reply state through 0x414810; otherwise it speaks the no-money line (0x418C40, group 2000). Not built.

name: dialog no money refusal

name: trainer skill list options
reason: Dialog reply case of the dispatcher 0x414810 for the trainer marker: says the NPC class line 3000, then builds one option per listed skill (basic skill name below 12, technological name from 12) with state 6, plus a closing forget-it line. Not implemented: our dialog blocks this reply marker as an unsupported interaction.

name: trainer offer for chosen skill
reason: Chosen skill of a trainer: a skill the PC already has trained gives refusal line 4000; one the training setter would refuse (probed by setting apprentice then resetting none) gives refusal 5000; else it offers apprentice training for 100 gold through the price step 0x418A40 (state 7). Not implemented: our dialog blocks this reply marker as an unsupported interaction.

name: trainer perform apprentice training
reason: Perform step of a trainer: sets the chosen skill (basic below 12, technological from 12) to apprentice on the PC through the training setter, ignores the setter's answer, then says class line 6000 with a single continue option. No trainer exists in our dialog.

name: tell rumors from list
reason: Rumor reply: drops from the reply's list every rumor that is quelled (0x4C5650) or already known to the PC (0x4C58D0); none left says line 7000, one left tells it at once (0x4190E0), several pick one at random (0x4CEF00) and offer the rest as options of state 9. Not implemented: the r: reply marker is blocked in our dialog.

name: tell one rumor and log it
reason: Takes the rumor's text (0x4C5700), speaks it as the NPC line with names substituted, marks the rumor known to the PC (0x4C57E0) and offers the class continue option. Not implemented: no rumor reply exists in our dialog (only the ru and rq conditions and the logging command).

name: dialogue insult option
reason: only the phrase (PC class line 3000); the option keeps the conversation runtime's insult transition

name: dialogue insult
reason: the NPC's generated reply is not built (the talk ends as Insulted; the insult phrase is 0x419190's); an insult reply whose action ends with JO, UW, FL or ET is offered blocked, where the original skips the insult (read for FL); ME operands other than 0 and 1 stop as unsupported

name: greeting builder
reason: states without an owner read as not that state (the host's facts); a slot index of 10 or more is ignored where the original writes past its arrays; slot 9 off keeps only this conversation's previous line; every node a slot names is planned with the g: node (a missing, reply, greeting or unplannable one stops or fails it even when its slot never fires; none installed)

name: greeting slot override applied
reason: With flag 1 the slot floats a node: stores the node, builds its line as floating speech and sets the end state 4; with flag 4 it continues at the node as an ordinary entry (state 0, rebuilds the replies); otherwise returns 0. Our Greet does the jump and float outcomes (Admit then Enter, or the floating line then Finish) but not as a separate function and without the dialog record's state numbers. Nearest code: the greeting jump and float outcomes are handled inside DialogConversation.Greet (a private step that already carries 0x416840) with the dialog record's state numbers left out, so no method of ours is this function.

name: healer menu
reason: The healer reply: NPC class line 14000, then by the NPC's heal skill level (0x4B1AB0) options of state 12 and 13, spell options for spells 60, 61, 62 and 64 at the top level, the skill service of 0x419A00 (skill 10) when allowed (0x4AE570), and forget-it. Not implemented, the h: reply stays blocked.

name: skill service option
reason: Builds a player option naming the skill (basic name below 12, technological from 12) with state 14 and the skill number as value, from PC line range 900 to 999. Part of the healer and skill service menus, not implemented.

name: spell service option
reason: Builds a player option naming a spell (0x4B1600) with state 15 and the spell number, from PC line range 1000 to 1099; used by the healer menu and the spell reply marker. Not implemented, the z: and h: replies are blocked.

name: skill service offer
reason: Skill service chosen from a menu: when the NPC's leader is the PC (0x45DE00) the service is performed at once for free through 0x419CB0, otherwise it offers the service at the price of the skill's service (0x4C62D0 or 0x4C69E0 from the NPC's level and trained rank) through the price step 0x418A40 (state 16). Not implemented.

name: spell service offer
reason: Spell chosen from a healer menu: a follower of the PC casts it at once for free through 0x419D50, anyone else offers it at the spell's price (0x4B1740) through the price step 0x418A40 (state 17). Not implemented.

name: perform skill service
reason: Performs a skill service on the PC: picks the item for skills 10 and 14 (0x4C91F0), sets a forced-success request flag 0x2000 when the NPC is not controlled (0x45DDA0 is zero) and starts the use-skill goal (0x4350F0), then says class line 15000. Not implemented in our dialog.

name: perform spell service
reason: Casts a spell for the PC as a service: builds a cast record (0x455A20) with the PC as target (0x4440E0), adds the forced bit 2 when the NPC is not controlled (0x45DDA0 zero), starts the cast (0x455AC0), then says class line 15000. Not implemented, no dialog spell service exists.

name: drop known towns from list
reason: Compacts a list of area numbers in place keeping those the PC does not know (0x4CAF50 false) and returns how many are left. The filter feeds the town directions pages; not implemented, our dialog has no directions reply.

name: town directions page
reason: Splits the reply's comma list of areas, drops the known ones (0x419E20), says an NPC line (100 range, 500 range with the flag) and builds a page of four options named by the areas (0x4CAE90) of state 19 (22 with the flag), then a more option of state 18 (21) while entries remain, else forget-it. Not implemented.

name: town directions step
reason: Parses the reply's response; a positive value is the price in gold and builds the price step 0x418A40 (state 20), with none it goes straight to the direction line 0x41A150. Not implemented.

name: town direction line
reason: Says where a town lies: the direction (0x4B8D50) and distance (0x4B96F0) from the NPC to the area's location (0x4CAED0), divided by 3168, choose NPC line base 200 (under 2), 300 (under 100) or 400, plus 10 per direction. Does not make the area known. Not implemented.

name: town reveal step
reason: Same shape as 0x41A0F0 for the learning variant: a positive value is the price and builds the price step (state 23), else it goes to the reveal line 0x41A290. Not implemented.

name: town reveal line and learn
reason: Like 0x41A150 with line bases 600 (under 2) and 700 and the area name formatted into the text, then makes the area known to the PC (0x4CAFD0). Not implemented, so a dialog cannot teach a town.

name: story news reply
reason: Reply case that builds the NPC line through 0x41A440, the class continue option and the response step. Not implemented, the c: reply is blocked.

name: story news line
reason: Chooses the NPC line from the story state (0x445090): the NPC script's override line 10000 + state first, else a line of message file chosen by the NPC's gender (stat 26) and the PC's gender, at 25 per story state plus the PC's race stat. Not implemented.

name: newspaper menu
reason: Builds the newspaper reply: NPC lines 4200 to 4299 and options to buy the current issue (queue word 4 through 0x4BF200, state 28), hear its headline (state 26), ask for older issues (state 27) and forget-it. The newspaper queue is stored by our session but no reply shows it.

name: newspaper current headline
reason: Puts the current issue's headline text (0x460800) into the NPC line with a closing stop, adds a line from the 4300 range, and offers to buy it (state 28) or forget it. Not implemented.

name: newspaper older issues list
reason: Collects the four reserved queue words (0x4BF200 for 0 to 3) that are not -1; with none says line 4400 range, else lists each issue's headline as an option of state 28. Not implemented.

name: newspaper price step
reason: Parses the reply's response and builds the price step 0x418A40 for buying the chosen issue at 2 gold (state 29). Not implemented.

name: newspaper issue given
reason: Creates the newspaper item for the chosen issue (0x4BF210) and moves it to the PC (0x4617F0), then says class line 15000. Not implemented.

name: sound id lookup
reason: the path it builds is checked as a virtual path (too long or non-ASCII or rooted or with .. is refused) where the original builds it unchecked

name: voice channel change
reason: only the channel volume from the setting; flattening live voice is the backend's

name: music channel change
