name: missing art table init
reason: Loads the missing-art masks (10 critter masks, one per monster, one per unique NPC) from the file, and when the load fails rebuilds them by testing whether the art file of each of 19 animation and weapon pairs exists, logging each miss, and saves the file. Our MissingMasks rebuilds from the held art names the same way but never saves a file.

name: missing art table load
reason: Reads the header and compares it with the current count of critter, monster and unique NPC art files (0x41D390), then reads the three mask arrays and compares each read length (the unique NPC one with the unique count); any short read or mismatch returns failure so the init rebuilds. Our load checks the header and total length only.

name: missing art mask file load and check
reason: Opens the missing-art mask file, reads its header and requires it to equal the file count of 0x41D390, then reads the critter, monster and unique NPC mask tables, each compared with its own list count, and returns 1 only when every read is complete. Ours reads the same header and masks from the content stack and rebuilds them by file checks on a mismatch, but never writes the rebuilt file back and has no loaded flag; the rebuild and save are the caller 0x41CE60.

name: art file count of critter folders
reason: Counts the art files in every subfolder of the critter, monster and unique NPC art folders (skipping dot entries), the number the missing-art mask header must equal. Ours counts names that the content stack holds one folder below those three roots and ending in .art; the original lists real folders, ours the merged archive and loose names. Nearest code: the count only serves the missing-art mask header; our AreaDataOwner.MissingMasks counts the names the content stack holds inline (CritterFile is a name test, not this count).

name: art id normalisation callback
reason: Art name callback that dispatches on the art type (15 types) and rewrites the id before any name is built: for critters elf female becomes human body, plate armour forces male and maps elf to human and halfling to dwarf, then the missing-art repair 0x41DA40 and the weapon, shield and explode, stunned, walk and run clearing rules; monsters and unique NPCs without the body rules; the other types reset frame, rotation or palette. Ours does the critter, monster and unique NPC branches while building the file name; the other type branches are not a separate normaliser (walls, tiles, scenery have their own code).

name: missing art animation repair
reason: Does nothing until the masks are loaded or for a critter number outside the list; otherwise tries 19 checked animation and weapon pairs in order and, for a set mask bit whose animation (and for low attack its weapon) matches, replaces the animation (walk, run to walk; stunned to stand; ten low attacks to attack; death variants to fall down; stealth walk to walk), setting weapon 0 or 1 for the walk and stand cases. Ours reproduces the pair loop and replacements but loads the masks lazily, so the masks-not-loaded no-op never occurs.

name: art name of an art id
reason: only ART type 15: the callback names no file (error 0x10), so the ART cache 0x51AA90 returns -1, frame data 0x5031C0 fails and the object draw gets an empty rectangle; only the id 0xFFFFFFFF on an object other than a wall or portal is admitted as no body, other type-15 ids stay refused

name: path request
reason: the gate, the direct attempt (0x41F840) and the 64 x 64 search (0x41F9F0) over the caller's tests (IOriginalPathMap), shared by the drop, the click route and its corridor (DC2-DC4, LR1); flag 0x1 is an argument (its stale window cost, LRA3, not modelled), flags 0x20, 0x200, 0x400 (fire) and 0x1000 are not modelled

name: path flags to traversal mode
reason: Maps the path request flag bits to the object traversal mode: bit 0x2 gives 1, 0x4 gives 2, 0x10 gives 4 (the mode in which PCs and NPCs never block), used by the direct walk and the search. Our path map hardwires the mode per caller (the drop uses mode 4 in its own code) and has no flag-to-mode function; the start also holds 0x41F590, an unreferenced helper that turns a string of rotations into an end-tile delta and logs an unknown rotation.

name: path away from target
reason: Builds the away path used by the back-off and escape: from the request, tries eight directions at offsets 4, 5, 3, 6, 2, 7, 1, 0 from the direction toward the target, each a range-minus-distance line tested by the straight walk 0x41F840 with the line flag 0x800, takes the first success, else retries the line with the most partial steps. Ours holds the offset table (the property AwayOffsets) and the interface AwayTile, but the world host's AwayTile always returns no tile, so no away line is ever walked.

name: straight walk path attempt
reason: The direct attempt of the path request: 0 when the larger axis distance exceeds 32, otherwise steps one rotation at a time toward the target, writing each rotation, stopping at a blocked tile, a refused object traversal or window piece, a trap the mover avoids, or (flag 0x400) fire; success returns the step count, less one with the into-goal flag, failure stores the completed steps in field 0x24. Ours omits flag 0x8 (skip tile test), flag 0x40 (accept every step, the flight), the fire check, the traversal mode from 0x41F570 and uses the buffer length instead of the request's step budget as the step limit.

name: bounded grid path search
reason: The fallback search of the path request: 64 by 64 window centred on both tiles, best-first by cost plus ten times the larger axis distance, entry cost 10 (90 onto an avoided trap), plus 50 across a window piece, plus 1 per turn, dropping tiles whose estimate exceeds the budget, rotations written from the start and the result capped at 8. For an NPC mover it also limits searches to 11 per 1000 ms and 250 ms of search time per window, failing over budget. Ours reproduces the window, costs and pruning (with BestFirst.Run) but has no NPC search budget, no flag 0x8 or mode handling.

name: straight line path samples
reason: Original: A second copy of the line sampler 0x4201C0 (same steps: both tiles to screen centres, the pixel line in 10-pixel samples through 0x4203B0 and 0x420330, then a last sample for the leftover points); the path request 0x41F3C0 calls it for request flag 0x80 and returns the sample count (0 when the line is longer than the buffer). Ours: LineOfFireRules.Samples computes the identical line, but no path request takes the flag 0x80 branch (the registry row of the path request 0x41F3C0 lists the flags 0x20, 0x200, 0x400 and 0x1000 as not modelled and does not name 0x80); the straight-line retry of a walk is RoutePlanner.StraightRetry.

name: run handle lookup
reason: Original: Finds the run table slot whose run matches a 12-byte run handle (slot index, run id, change counter): scans the 216 slots with the handle comparison 0x421CE0; returns the slot or answers false and clears the out pointer; a null handle id is not looked up. Ours: GoalRunTable.TryGet finds a run by (slot, run id); the change counter is network-only and not kept. It carries no address mark.

name: animation module load wrapper
reason: Original: module load entry of the animation run table: raises the loading flag, calls the run table reader 0x422520, clears the flag, recounts the significant runs and logs a mismatch. Ours: the save does not read or write goal runs; run-local goal runs restart from the AI tick (documented limit, PS15).

name: idle test
reason: the object's art animation (the art id's animation, 0x503E20) is the caller's; an owner with no run is not idle where the original addresses memory before the run table

name: goal stepper
reason: the node steps, the 8-goal stack, the 100-node limit and the end step's pending charge (EX6 switch) over the executor's goals, with the cast's attempt goals' end node (0x429CD0) on a pop and the end step; the other end nodes' animation clean-up, the interrupt test and the subturn hook after a run are the host's

name: goal next frame
reason: queues the run's next step the frame delay x8 after the animation clock now (no -animcatchup) and records the due time on the run; the -animcatchup branch (relative to the previous due time through 0x45BA30, flag 0x5DE6D0) is not followed, and the step's own work (the nodes) is the host's

name: goal pop
reason: Original: The stepper's pop: marks the run done when its bottom goal pops without the keep flag, runs the popped goal's end node (unless the step word says to skip it) after refreshing the frame's parameters, clears the run's path state unless the step word keeps it, uncounts the significant goal, lowers the depth and makes the parent the current goal (at the bottom it marks the run done). Ours: The pop is a branch of AiExecutorRules.Step (frames are removed after EndNode, the run ends Finished at the bottom); the keep-flags and path-reset bits of the step word and the parent's restart are not separate, and the goal queue of a cast uses GoalStartRules; no method of its own.

name: significant goal recount
reason: Original: Walks all in-use runs and counts the goals on their stacks whose type has priority 2 or more and no no-interrupt flag (asserting each goal type in range, the bad-type path frees the run). Ours: GoalRunTable.SignificantGoalCount derives exactly this count from the table's runs instead of keeping a counter; no address mark.

name: kill every run of an object
reason: the gate that skips the kill while the light-scheme hour runs (0x4A7FB0) is the caller's; the end nodes and events of the killed runs are the caller's

name: interrupt every run of an object
reason: the network branch (the interrupt first sent to the other side) is not followed; the end nodes and events of the ended runs are the caller's

name: interrupt every run at map end
reason: the sweep over the table is complete; each run it interrupts goes through GoalRunTable.Interrupt, which is partial (the end nodes, the events and the stepper's subturn hook are the caller's)

name: interrupt every run at a level
reason: the sweep over the table is complete; each run it interrupts goes through GoalRunTable.Interrupt, which is partial (the end nodes, the events and the stepper's subturn hook are the caller's)

name: interrupt every run at round start
reason: the sweep over the table is complete; each run it interrupts goes through GoalRunTable.Interrupt, which is partial (the end nodes, the events and the stepper's subturn hook are the caller's)

name: remove animated eye candy
reason: Remove interrupts every matching run and counts them; the original stops at the first interrupt that answers success and always answers 1. The anyTag option is the static remove's

name: eye candy duplicate test
reason: Original: Answers whether the owner already runs a goal-45 run whose current frame has the same normalised art and the same tag; used by the eye-candy add for the duplicate flag 0x80. Ours: AreaEyeCandyHost.Play refuses a duplicate in its own check (documented in its summary); the test has no method or address mark of its own.

name: start goal on another object
reason: Original: Starter used by doors and spell missiles: in a network client it does nothing; otherwise it builds a frame for the goal on the target object (0x44D4E0, which interrupts the object's runs at level 3), copies the caller frame's slots 1 to 20, writes the object's current art and the starter as slot 4 and starts the run (0x44D520); answers whether the run started. Ours: IAiDoorWorld.StartDoorRun (AreaDoorHost.StartDoorRun) starts the door's 70 or 71 run and AreaMissileHost.Launch starts goal 28 on the missile; the generic copy of the frame slots is not a method of its own.

name: spell missile create
reason: Launch creates the missile entity at the start tile through GameSessionOwner.CreateMissile and starts its goal-28 run; the prototype, the do-not-light flag, the art facing and the light and sound attachment are not done there (the viewer draws and lights the missile)

name: projectile facing node
reason: Original: Goal 36 node 4: computes the facing art of the projectile from the shooter's tile toward the target through 0x4B6A00 and 0x4B6B10 and discards the result; fails only for a missing projectile or shooter. Ours: IAiProjectileWorld.ProjectileFace (documented with this address) is implemented by AreaProjectileHost.ProjectileFace as a presence test; the interface member carries the address, the host method does not.

name: missile destroy node
reason: Original: Goal 28 node 6: unless the missile object is already destroyed, hides it (object flag 0x2) for most arts and destroys it. Ours: IAiMissileWorld.MissileDestroy (documented with this address) is implemented by AreaMissileHost.MissileDestroy through the session's DestroyMissile; the art-class exception that skips the hide is not modelled.

name: object on destination node
reason: LegEnd carries the test for goal 28 only (a missile off its destination flies its line again); goal 43's test is IAiKnockbackWorld.KnockbackAtDestination and the pickup's and goal 7's are the executor's own

name: please move step choice
reason: Original: Node 1 of goal 68 (please move): from the critter's tile tries the eight neighbours starting at a random rotation and takes the first whose step is clear (0x425760), else the first one occupied by a critter that accepts a please-move request (0x4363E0), then sets the global delay to 1000 ms; writes the tile as the goal's destination (slot 6). Ours: Goal 68 is only a descriptor (GoalDescriptors); no executor runs it, so a follower or NPC asked to step aside does not choose a neighbour tile this way.

name: within range and step clear node
reason: Original: Goal node used by goals 8, 33, 38 and 81: answers true when the distance between the object and the target (Chebyshev, 0x4B96F0) is at most the frame's range and the first step toward it is clear (0x425840); false when either slot is empty. Ours: The executor's own range test plus IAiGoalWorld.FirstStepClear (AreaAiHost.FirstStepClear, documented with the step test 0x425130 and the flight's test 0x425840) cover it; no method carries the mark.

name: location within range node
reason: Original: Goal node (goals 39 and 41, the use of an item on a tile): answers true when the distance from the object to the location in slot 1 is at most the frame's range. Ours: No goal of ours runs the item-on-tile use; the range test is an executor inline.

name: follow within range plus two node
reason: Original: Follow-goal node: answers true when the distance between the follower and its leader is at most the frame's range plus 2 (then the follow pushes a walk, else a run). Ours: AiExecutorRules.FollowNode decides the follower's walk or run from its own distance test; no method carries the mark.

name: walk replan trigger node
reason: Original: Goal 5 node 5: when path flag 0x4 or 0x8 is set, clears the step state (0x430FC0), copies the run's pace, marks needs plan (path flag 0x1 set, 0x4 cleared) and clears run flags 0x30; sets run flag 0x2 when flag 0x8 is set (outside a network client). Ours: The retarget is GoalRunTable.RetargetDestination and the hero's run host (GT214); the node itself has no method.

name: walk retarget check node
reason: Original: Goal node: sets path flag 0x4 when the frame's destination differs from the location of the target object in slot 1, then does what 0x425430 does when 0x4 or 0x8 is set (replan, else answers false). Ours: Same as 0x425430: retargeting is GoalRunTable.RetargetDestination; the replan flag is not a separate method.

name: ranged approach callback
reason: the stop decision only (EX9 switch); the target-moved test is the walk goal's and the range write is the executor's

name: step blocked test
reason: Original: Answers whether the step to a neighbouring tile is blocked: first the mover's mode flags (0x4257E0), then the tile test (0x4D7110), then the object traversal test (0x43FD70). Ours: IOriginalPathMap.TileBlocked and Traverse model the two tests of a path request; the executor's FirstStepClear asks the host for a step; no method carries the mark.

name: walker traversal mode flags
reason: Original: Builds the mode bits of a walking object: flag 0x20000 sets bits 3, cannot open doors (0x45F550) sets 1 and cannot jump windows (0x45F570) sets 2; the bits feed the tile and traversal tests. Ours: The mover's capabilities are the host's facts (IOriginalPathMap); the registry notes our window jump rule is more permissive for 0x45F570.

name: flight step clear test
reason: Original: Answers whether the step from an object toward another is clear for the flight test: the tile test with the traversal flags, then a trial that marks the target non-blocking, tests the object traversal (0x43FDC0) and clears the mark again; blocked only by something other than the target. Ours: IAiGoalWorld.FirstStepClear(ignoreTarget) is documented with this address and implemented by AreaAiHost.FirstStepClear; no method carries the mark.

name: wander destination planner
reason: Original: Node of the wander goal: unless a network client, picks a random tile within the frame's range of the critter's wander location, derives the path budget (0x426320) and path request (0x425BF0, 0x41F3C0 with a retry in flag 1), stores the tile as destination, and on failure ends the subturn of a non-PC in a round (0x4B7C90). Ours: No counterpart: no executor runs goal 65 and the standpoint step (NpcRouteOutcome.AtStandpoint) starts no wander, so a wandering NPC stands still.

name: path request mode set up
reason: Original: Fills the mode flags of a path request for a PC or NPC: 0x2 cannot open doors, 0x4 cannot jump windows, 0x200 when a critter property (0x45EDE0) holds and basic skill 6 is untrained, 0x400 when its fire resistance (0x43D6D0) is below 45 and a stat check (0x4B0490) is nonzero, 0x10 when the argument is set and the critter is not in combat mode (0x4B3D50); answers 0 for an entangled critter. Ours: AreaAiHost.PlanPath refuses an entangled critter (GT149); the doors, windows and fire modes are the path map's facts, and the flags 0x200 and 0x400 are not modelled.

name: wander dark destination planner
reason: Original: Node of the seek-darkness wander goal: like 0x425930 it picks a random destination in range and plans it, here sampling the light (0x4D9240) to prefer a dark tile. Ours: Not modelled: no executor runs goal 66 (descriptor only).

name: walk path step
reason: the PC's straight-line retry with flags 0x78 (LR4); the plan itself is RoutePlanner.Plan and the follower keeps the straight line for the rest of the walk (run flag 0x400)

name: path length query
reason: Original: Plans a path from an object to a location through 0x426500 in mode 0 and answers its length (0 when none); the move cost estimate 0x4B7BA0 uses it. Ours: TurnBasedRules.MoveCost takes the path length as an argument and the host's path plan (AreaAiHost.PlanPath) supplies it; no method carries the mark.

name: path length query b
reason: Original: The same query as 0x4261E0 with the mode 1 (the step onto the destination is not tested); used by the move cost estimate. Ours: As 0x4261E0.

name: walk path budget
reason: the first-plan branch, min(4 x distance + 5, 200), which every plan of a walk takes since a pop clears the field between plans (LR2); the 5 more of a second plan in the same call is not modelled

name: path search for a walker
reason: Original: Builds the search record for one walker (start, target, budget from 0x426320 or 200 with request flag 0x1000, flags from the walker: art bit 0x20000 gives 0x6, no portal capability 0x2, no window jump 0x4, a concealed walker with no skill-6 training 0x200), shifts the start one tile along the facing when the walker is mid-step (dropped when that tile is blocked or not traversable), asks the flag builder 0x425BF0 and runs the path request 0x41F3C0; stores the length and the walk's start and target on the run, clears the run's low flag bits and answers 1, else ends a non-player subturn and answers 0. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.Simulation.Navigation.RoutePlanner.Plan (the plan itself); the start-tile shift, the flag bits and the dead-walker subturn end are spread over the walk hosts with no method of their own.

name: spell missile path
reason: the leg's line is the combat projectile's (0x4201C0); a missile already on its destination arrives before a line is built (0x424D90)

name: knockback line node
reason: KnockbackRules.Line builds the line and LineRotation the rotation; storing them on the run and clearing the flag bits is AreaKnockbackHost.KnockbackBuildLine's (unmarked)

name: projectile line node
reason: Original: Node 6 of the projectile goal 36: builds the pixel line (0x4201C0) from the projectile's tile to the destination into the run's buffer, resets the step index and clears the low flag bits; fails when the line is refused. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.World.AreaProjectileHost.ProjectileBuildLine (ProjectileRules.Launch builds the flight); the address is cited only on the port interface IAiProjectileWorld.

name: escape path start
reason: EscapeDestination gives the destination only; the plan, the no-flee mark, the turn and the subturn end are the move away goal's host (AreaAiHost) code with no method of its own

name: concealed shown test
reason: Original: Node test of the critter-state, walk and attack goals: true for a player character or NPC (type 15 or 16) that is not the player's (0x40DA20 false) and whose art shows animation 5 (the concealed pose); the goal then pushes the unconceal goal 54. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.StunNode and DyingNode read Mover.Concealed and Pc with the constant ConcealedAnimation = 5; no method of its own.

name: stun countdown node
reason: Original: Stun countdown node (slot 7 of goal 57): outside a round it takes one from the counter in the run's frame slot 18 after each full play of the stun animation; at 0 or below it clears the stunned bit (field 0xDA, bit 0x20) and ends the goal; in a round the decrement is skipped (the round's skipped turns take 3 each through 0x427000) and the count test still applies. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.StunNode (the in-code comment cites 0x426F60); no method of its own.

name: turn based stun countdown
reason: The participant and stunned-bit tests are the round loop's caller (GameSessionOwner round code), not this method; ours looks at the first run's bottom goal instead of the lookup of the goal 57 run, and refuses while that run is being stepped

name: walk step check
reason: a living PC or NPC checked only before a segment's last step, the run ending on a hit (LR5): ARC-WORLD-073 follows it in the click route's follower under the Original switch SegmentEndCritterEndsWalk (no method of its own; the 0-300 ms delay before the run ends is not modelled); the PC's walk through other critters outside combat mode is ARC-WORLD-074's step admission (AreaGridSession.CrittersPass); a companion's walk passes them since ARC-WORLD-075 (AreaCompanion.PassesCritters) and its approach walk (goal 61) stops there under the same switch and plans again (LR11, docs/research/ledger/world.md#companion-walks-through-critters-arc-world-075); the trap spot before each step (TT10, docs/research/ledger/technology.md#trap-state-arc-world-076) is not implemented

name: walker door test node
reason: Original: Node 7 of the walker goals: takes the step direction from the path (or the object's rotation when the run has the first-plan flag) and asks the traversal door test 0x440700 whether a closed portal lies on the next step; on a hit it writes the portal handle into the current frame and answers true. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.World.AreaAiHost.ClosedDoorOn (port IAiGoalWorld.ClosedDoorOn carries the address); the host method has no mark.

name: window edge piece test
reason: Original: Looks for a window wall piece on the step's edge: on the object's own tile (when asked) and on the neighbour tile in the step direction, it reads the objects there and tests the wall piece kinds 9 to 20 against the facing; on a hit it gives the window object back and answers true. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.Data.Traversal.AreaStepSnapshot (the WindowJump edge rule); no method of its own.

name: walker window test node
reason: Original: Node 6 of the walker goals: takes the step direction as the door test does and asks the window edge test 0x4273B0 for the object on the step; on a hit it writes the window handle into the current frame and answers true (the window jump goal 14 follows). Ours: Nearest: AreaAiHost step handling (AiStepBlock) and AreaStepSnapshot window rule; no method of its own.

name: move near tile planner
reason: Original: Node 5 of goal 7 (walk to a tile, the script walk): plans from the object's tile to the frame's tile with the walk's budget, first with request flag 0 and then, when that finds no path, with flag 1 (the path may end on an occupied or blocked tile); on success clears the run's low flag bits and turns the walker; with no path a non-player's subturn ends. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.RunToTileNode (the comment cites 0x427730); the second request with flag 1 is the walk host's AreaAiHost.PlanPath; no method of its own.

name: approach path step
reason: the follow goal's move-near and run-near legs plan with the walk's flags and its budget, so outside combat mode critters do not block the plan (LR10): ARC-WORLD-075 follows it in the companion's route source and step admission (AreaCompanion.PassesCritters, no method of its own); the node's range, target and multiplayer branches were not read

name: attack approach plan
reason: the route to the target's tile with flag 0x1, one step short, with the walk's first budget and critters blocking (AP1-AP4); the first request without flag 0x1, which the gate refuses for a living target, and the range shortening, a no-op for range 1, are not modelled

name: portal valid node
reason: Original: First node of the door goals 11, 12, 49 and 50 (and shared by use and talk goals): true when the object is not destroyed or off (field 0x13 bits 0x3 clear) and is a portal (type 1); otherwise the goal pops. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.DoorNode (IAiDoorWorld.DoorValid); no method of its own.

name: portal closed and idle node
reason: Original: Second node of the door goals: the portal is valid (not destroyed or off, field 0x13 bits 0x3 clear), closed (0x4F08C0 says not open) and owns no main run (0x423300), so no door run is under way. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.ClosedAndIdle over IAiDoorWorld.DoorValid, DoorOpen and DoorBusy.

name: locked sound recheck node
reason: Original: Node 7 of the attempt-open-door goal 12: repeats the portal open attempt (0x4AEB70 with the opener and the door's rotation) and, when it refuses, plays the locked sound (0x4F1010) on the door; answers true when the objects are valid. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.DoorNode (IAiDoorWorld.DoorRefusesOpen and the Locked sound); no method of its own.

name: door close allowed node
reason: Original: Node 3 of the attempt-close-door goal 50: true unless the portal's flags (field 0x2E) hold the magically held bit 0x4; no action points, script or lock test. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.DoorNode (IAiDoorWorld.DoorHeld).

name: opener portal capability node
reason: Original: Node 3 of goal 12: true when the opener's art may handle portals at all (0x45F550) and the open attempt (0x4AEB70, run for its side effects such as the unlock script) answers zero; false otherwise. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.DoorNode (IAiDoorWorld.DoorOpenerCapable).

name: door open refused node
reason: Original: Node 3 of the open-door goal 11 (and node 4 of 12): true when the door is not destroyed or off and the opener's open attempt (0x4AEB70) answers non-zero; the attempt runs here and again in the next node. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.DoorNode (IAiDoorWorld.DoorRefusesOpen).

name: door attempt repeat node
reason: Original: Node 4 of goals 11 and 12 (and node 5 of 12): when the door is valid it runs the open attempt (0x4AEB70) once more for its side effects and always answers false, so the unlock script runs twice for a refused door. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.DoorNode; the double attempt is not reproduced as a separate step.

name: window jump allowed node
reason: Original: Node 11 of the walkers: true when the walker's art can jump windows (0x45F570) and, for a window portal in the frame, the open attempt (0x4AEB70) does not refuse; a window with no portal passes. Ours: Nearest: AreaAiHost step handling over AreaStepSnapshot's window rule (the jump goal 14 itself is not a run of ours).

name: use range node
reason: Original: First node of the use goals 38 and 81: checks that the user and the target are not null and writes the frame's range word: 1 for a container, a player character or an NPC (type 2, 15, 16), 2 for every other type. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.HeroUseNode (AiHeroTarget.UseRange); no method of its own.

name: use object act node
reason: Original: Last node of the use goals 38 and 81: charges 2 action points (0x4B7CD0), runs the access test 0x425840 again (blocked ends the run; it does not turn the user) and then acts by the target's type: a container or a creature opens the loot window for the local player (0x4EE310; not for a user with spell flag 0x20000 or a target with a main run), a bed shows the rest window (0x460820), anything else runs the object's use script (point 1, 0x441980) whose answer is ignored. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.HeroUseNode (the use goal's last step) and IAiDoorWorld.UseDoor for portals; the container, bed and loot branches are viewer code.

name: use item node
reason: Original: Last node of the item-use goal 39: when the item is still held by the user (0x4612A0) it calls the item use 0x462CC0 with the user, the item and the target; answers true then. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.UseItemNode (the comment cites 0x428CD0) over UseItemNow.

name: use item with skill node
reason: Only the healing case is run: HealWithItem covers the hero's heal-by-item chain (its documentation cites 0x4352C0/0x428E10); other skills used through an item are not wired

name: use item on tile node
reason: Original: Last node of the use-item-on-tile goal 41: when the item is held by the user (0x4612A0) it calls the tile item use 0x462FC0 with the user, the item and the tile; answers true then (hero only). Ours: No counterpart; nearest: the viewer's item use on a tile (no mark); NPCs never start goal 41.

name: use item on tile skill node
reason: Original: Node of goal 42 (use an item on a tile with a skill): refuses null objects, a destroyed or off item and an item the user does not hold, fills a skill invocation (skill, modifier, tile, flag bit from the frame) and runs the skill check 0x4C7160. Ours: No counterpart; the hero's item-on-tile skill use is not a goal of ours.

name: move away set no flee node
reason: Original: Node 7 of the move away goal 52: runs when the objects are valid, clears the flee state with set no flee (0x4AF1D0) on the NPC and answers true (the cornered end of the flight). Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules (the move away step calls world.SetNoFlee, the comment at ExecutorRules.cs cites the cornered end); no method of its own.

name: attack target alive node
reason: Original: Node 1 of the attack goals 18 and 20: true unless the target is a player character or NPC (type 15 or 16) that is dead (0x45D8D0); a dead target pops the goal with no end step. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.CombatApproachNode and AttackNode (the comment cites 0x429450; world.DeadCritter); the hero's AiHeroAttackTarget.Dead; no method of its own.

name: attack possible node
reason: Original: Node 2 of the attack goal 18 (node 4 of the kill goal 20): asks attack possible (0x4294F0) for the attacker and target; when it is not possible and a round is active (0x4B6D70) the attacker's subturn ends (0x4B7C90), and the answer passes on. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.AttackPossible over the caller's facts (registry row 0x4294F0); the subturn end is the executor's CombatApproachNode and AttackNode, which have no mark.

name: attack possible
reason: over the caller's facts: activity, Body of Air, the target's state, the line of fire's foreign blocker and the path test (0x426500) are the world's

name: approach sound and path clear node
reason: Original: Node 7 of the combat approach goal 79: plays the sound in the goal's sound slot (+0x98, through 0x41B930) when set, then clears that slot in every frame of the run's stack so the sound plays once; answers true. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.CombatApproachNode (the approach sound is not played by the executor); no method of its own.

name: attack repeat test node
reason: Original: Node 12 of the attempt attack goal 19: true only for a player character in combat mode with auto attack, a target neither destroyed, off, dead nor busted, run flag 0x800 clear, no round, the attacker's non-lethal bit clear and no boomerang away; it then clears the run's walk budget and low flags so the goal waits 5 ms and attacks again, else the goal ends. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.AttackNode default branch (an NPC's goal ends); the hero's HeroAttackRepeats port is a default false (viewer repeats it); no method of its own.

name: fidget continue node
reason: Original: Node 5 of the fidget goal 2: true when the idler is in combat mode; otherwise only when its critter flag 0xDB bit 0x2 is set and the distance to the local player character (0x441AE0) is below 30 tiles. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.FidgetAfterRun (the fidget start tests); this continue test has no method of its own.

name: attack goal reach test
reason: the distance at most the wielded weapon's range (at least 1) and the clear shot (line-of-fire cost below 26, no blocker but the target), for every weapon; the target's destroyed and off flags and the wielded-item lookup are the caller's

name: ranged weapon reach node
reason: Original: Node 8 of the combat approach goal 79: true when the wielded weapon's range (0x465E30) is above 1, which picks the ranged approach walk. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.CombatApproachNode (weapon range from the world's reach facts); no method of its own.

name: casting goal start
reason: the 4 action points through the session's charge and the pre-animation check (SpellCostRules.PreAnimationCost); the goal node machinery (rows, delays, the facing and get-up nodes) is the viewer's; Steamwoven frees a refused goal's run unpaid (MG39, MagicAnomalyProfile.GoalRefusalChargesBegin)

name: casting goal target node
reason: StartGoal ends the goal when the target is destroyed or switched off, as one part of the casting goal start (the method's own mark is 0x429B50); the assert on an empty run slot and the read and drop of the target location are not reproduced

name: casting goal missile launch
reason: the missile art test (0x458B70), the secondary cast eye candy and the missile object (0x4248A0, goal 28) are the viewer's

name: casting goal release
reason: the target re-check and the BEGIN; the eye candy and the goal flags are the viewer's; both settings free the run of a failed re-check (MG41 fixed without a switch)

name: casting goal end
reason: the free with the BEGIN charged, skipped after the release frame or for a run whose BEGIN ran; the eye-candy removal and the animation reset are the viewer's; Steamwoven frees a refused goal's run unpaid (MG39, MagicAnomalyProfile.GoalRefusalChargesBegin) and charges only a run whose BEGIN would have paid (MG40, MagicAnomalyProfile.GoalEndChargesAnyRun, SessionSpellCaster.ChargeBegin)

name: spell missile goal end
reason: the missile object is the viewer's; the run of a lost missile is freed unpaid in both modes (MG44, owner decision 2026-10-28)

name: missile speed node
reason: Original: Node 8 of the shoot spell goal 28: reads the spell entry's missile speed (0x458CA0, the registry row 0x458CA0) into the run's frame slot 18; false when the run has no entry. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.World.AreaMissileHost.MissileSpeed (the port IAiMissileWorld.MissileSpeed carries the address; it only checks that the missile exists, the pace is SpellMissileRules.Pace).

name: casting play start
reason: BeginCast returns the swing (action frame and rest) and notices; the frame words are not stored as such; the extra missile pace after a release is added

name: casting animation start
reason: Original: Animation begin node (the shared start with its own debug text) used as node 12 of the cast-with-animation goal 83: picks the art (the frame's animation or the object's art), refuses a stoned, stunned or paralysed critter (flags 0x60) unless the animation is 0x11 to 0x13, plays the death sound when the frame is the dying goal, sets the art, reads its rate and stores the delay 1000 / rate (100 ms with a log when it cannot read) in +0xCFC; sets run flag 0x10 and answers true. Ours: Nearest: AreaAiHost.BeginCast (castAnimation true gives no play: NPC art is not read, so the release runs at once); no method of its own.

name: spell missile arrival test
reason: with the destination test 0x424D90 and the retarget 0x42BEC0; a target gone from the map counts as arrived

name: eye candy callback node
reason: Original: Callback node of the eye candy goals 47 and 48: calls the spell run action 0x457000 with the run's tag and phase 3 (callback) and answers true. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.OverlayNode (world.EyeCandyCallback(owner, tag, 3), IAiOverlayWorld); no method of its own.

name: eye candy end callback node
reason: Original: End callback node of the eye candy goals 58 and 59: calls the spell run action 0x457000 with the run's tag and phase 4 (end callback) and answers true. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.OverlayNode case 4 (world.EyeCandyCallback(owner, tag, 4)); no method of its own.

name: skill attempt node
reason: AttemptSkill is the invocation and its success flag only (heal skill and pick pocket); the target test and the 4 action points are AiExecutorRules.SkillAttempt's (unmarked); every other skill answers false

name: skill success flag node
reason: Original: Node 5 of the attempt pickpocket goal 86: answers the run flag 0x40000 (set by the check's success), which sends a success to the no-animation branch. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.AttemptSkillNode (the success flag skipsAnimation); no method of its own.

name: pickpocket skill test node
reason: Original: Node 7 of the use skill goal 33: true when the frame's skill is 5 (pick pocket), which replaces the goal by the attempt pickpocket goal 86. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.UseSkillNode (the skill choice of the attempt goal); no method of its own.

name: picklock skill test node
reason: Original: Node 5 of the use skill goal 33: true when the frame's skill is 14 (pick locks), which replaces the goal by the pick-locks attempt goal 67. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.UseSkillNode (the skill choice of the attempt goal); no method of its own.

name: pick locks attempt node
reason: Original: Node of the pick-locks goal 67: fills a skill invocation (skill from the frame, source, target, item, plant flag) and runs the skill check 0x4C7160 with no action point charge; answers true. Ours: AreaAiHost.AttemptPickLocks is an NOT READY stub (an NPC's lock picking does nothing); the hero's pick locks is the session's.

name: attempt attack hit node
reason: Original: Node 8 of the attempt attack goal 19 at its action frame: with the attacker, the target not destroyed or off and a hit location (frame +0x88) set, calls the attack hit step 0x4B3BB0 with them and answers true; otherwise false. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.World.AreaAiHost.Hit (port Hit, doc cites 0x42A630 on the port) over GameSessionOwner.AttackByNpc; no mark.

name: burning goal fire damage
reason: FireDamage is the round gate and the burn call; the victim list, the damage record and its path are AreaFireBurner and SessionSpellCaster.ApplyBurn (the burner's stat bonus is not read)

name: ranged attacker weapon test node
reason: Original: Node 9 of the attempt attack goal 19: true when the attacker is not destroyed or off and its wielded weapon's range (0x465E30) is above 1. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.AttackNode (Reach facts, weapon range); no method of its own.

name: pickup act node
reason: Original: Node 1 of the attempt pickup goal 16: when the picker and the item are set and the item is not destroyed or off (field 0x13 bits 0x3 clear) it runs the pickup 0x42AA70 and answers its result. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.AttemptPickupNode (the comment cites 0x42A9B0) with the port IAiGoalWorld.PickUp, which AreaAiHost leaves empty.

name: pickup into inventory
reason: Original: Moves the item into the picker's inventory: refuses unless the loot counter is clear (0x4681A0), the item is held by a junk pile (holder description 0xBCF) or free on the ground, then charges 1 action point (0x4B7CD0), plays the item sound for a local picker (0x4F0BF0, 0x41B930) and calls the item transfer 0x4617F0 (the local flag set outside a round or in a network round); also reached by the network packet handler. Ours: Nearest: Arcanum.World.AreaInventoryHost.PickUp (the hero's pickup); an NPC's pickup is the empty port AreaAiHost.PickUp; no mark.

name: throw item node
reason: ThrowItem calls the session's NPC throw with the item's weight and the struck critter; the thrown weapon's flight lands at once and some blockers on the line strike nothing (the method's own NOT READY)

name: talk validity node
reason: Original: Node 1 of the talk goal 21: true when the talker and the target are set, the target is not destroyed or off, neither has spell flag 0x10000, a critter talker or target is not stoned, stunned or paralysed (critter flags 0x60) and the target is a player character or NPC; false ends the run silently. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.HeroTalkNode (the hero's talk goal); NPCs never run goal 21; no method of its own.

name: talk range node
reason: Original: Node 4 of the talk goal 21: the target is not destroyed or off and the distance between the two (0x4B96F0) is strictly below the dialog range of the talker (0x4AFBB0: 5 for a player character, 10 for anyone else). Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.HeroTalkNode with AiHeroTarget.UseRange (the range is the hero's one value); no method of its own.

name: talk act node
reason: Original: Node 5 of the talk goal 21: with valid objects and no network client it calls the interface hook 0x460410 (which opens the dialog through the pointer 0x5E8694), and always answers 0, so the run takes the end step right after the call. Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.HeroTalkNode (the act of the talk goal, ARC-DEV-180) and the viewer's dialog start; no method of its own.

name: unconceal end node
reason: Original: End node of the unconceal goal 54: skipped for a killed run and while the map is being cleared; otherwise resets the object's art to animation 0 frame 0 and, for a player character or NPC, clears sneak (0x430490) and, unless its leader is concealed, sets concealment off for the group (0x45EE30). Ours: Nearest: AiExecutorRules.EndNode (goal 54's unconceal start is the host's Unconceal); the end node has no method of its own.

name: stand art end node
