Ours: AiExecutorRules.EyeCandyNode case 3 (plain comment) places the parts; CastEyeCandyAnimation's constructor and class comment carry the pace rule (the art built last) for the casting goals; light and sound are the viewer s (TerrainViewerEyeCandy).

name: eye candy finish
reason: Original: Finish node of the eye candy goals (45, 47, 58, 59, 75, 76): clears frame flag 0x40; for a looping entry (frame flag 0x80) or with all overlay slots empty answers false, so the begin runs again; otherwise clears the overlay entries and the light and answers true (the goal pops). Ours: AiExecutorRules.Finish (ExecutorEyeCandyGoals.cs, no comment of its own) and EyeCandyStepKind.Ended; the overlay is derived from the run, so no field is cleared.

name: reverse eye candy step
reason: EyeCandyFrameStep(reverse) does the frame arithmetic, the background step and the action flag; the light and the sound are the viewer s

name: reverse eye candy begin
reason: Original: Begin node of the reverse eye candy goals (46, 48, 59): as 0x4315B0 but the start frame is the last one (or a random frame from 1 with run flag 0x800). Ours: AiExecutorRules.EyeCandyNode case 3 with the reverse flag (plain comment); light and sound are the viewer s.

name: reverse eye candy finish
reason: Original: Finish node of the reverse eye candy goals (46, 48, 59): clears the overlay entries and the light (0x43ECF0, 0x43EE10) and answers as the forward finish (looping: false, else true). Ours: AiExecutorRules.Finish serves both directions (no comment of its own).

name: fire eye candy step
reason: EyeCandyFrameStep does the frame step; the damage is the fire host s (IAiFireWorld) and the mod 3 trigger is in the executor's node, not in this method

name: reverse fire eye candy step
reason: As 0x4322A0, with the reverse flag of EyeCandyFrameStep

name: attack animation begin
reason: the item event only: the attacker's attacks an opponent with the target after the checks and the action point charge (the host's); the animation and its speed are the host's, the attacking bark (1 in 4) is played by the viewer (ARC-RENDER-1126)

name: attack animation step
reason: Original: Frame step of the attempt attack goal (19): refusals (flag 0x10000, stunned or paralysed); header failure or the last frame resets the art and clears the playing flag; one frame before the action frame sets run flag 0x4; outside a round a critter in a swing animation (6, 10 or 8) at the right frame, with its target still valid and the attack possible (0x4294F0), re-faces the target and restarts the swing; after a restart recomputes the pause 1000 / the art rate through 0x42EE90 less 10 x (weapon speed - 10) and clamps it to 30..800. Ours: RealTimeCombatRules (AttackFramePauseMs, Begin and the update of a playing attack) carries the pause and the end rules with no address; ItemSpellTriggerEvents carries the begin 0x432700; the restart of a swing is not modelled as such.

name: wielded weapon ammunition test
reason: Original: Answers whether the attacker may attack with the weapon worn at location 1004: true when the weapon takes no ammunition type (10000), else when the units of that type the attacker carries are at least the weapon's per-shot consumption (field 126). Ours: GameSessionOwner.ShotAmmunition answers the same question for the hero's wielded weapon (type, per-shot count, short flag) and the NPC shot path builds its own ammunition tuple (GameSessionNpcAttack); neither names this address nor shares one test.

name: pool of blood creation
reason: the refusals only (violence filter, undead or mechanical, elemental, stoned); the multiplayer client, the network message, the editor's last frame and the failed goal's deletion are not modelled; the session creates the pool

name: hit blood eye candy
reason: Original: The damage effect of a hit on a struck PC or NPC: skipped on a multiplayer client, for a destroyed or off object, for a critter whose flag 0x100 forbids blood splotches and for types other than 15 and 16; picks the entry of the animation eye-candy list (0x5DE670) by the hit's kind or by the damage (above 5: 8, 10 or more: 9, 15 or more: 10; 6 and 7 by the gore filter 0x5DE6A4), runs it with limit 3 and ends by calling the spell hit effect 0x459A30. Ours: No counterpart: BloodPoolRules covers the pool left by a kill (0x432D90) only; the blood eye candy of a hit is not modelled; the spell hit effect 0x459A30 that it ends with is reached through the attack end (SessionSpellCaster.CritterHit).

name: goal end action point charge
reason: only the throw goal's charge: the local PC is exempt in the Original setting (CombatAnomalyProfile.PcThrowCostsNothing) and everyone else pays 2; the other five goals that share this end node charge through AiExecutorRules.ChargeSmall, which carries no mark, and the node's answer is the caller's

name: perform animation starter
reason: Original: Starter of the script action 62: asserts a set object and an animation of 0 to 25; a critter asked for animation 10 gets goal 60 (kneel, magic hands), any other object goal 0 with the animation; both through the priority-3 replacement 0x44D4E0 and no gate. Ours: AreaAiHost.ScriptAnimate with AiExecutorRules.PerformAnimationFrame does it for an NPC of the shown map; their comments name GT155 and not this address, and the hero and non-NPC objects have no path.

name: rotate starter
reason: the gates of the starter in the original's order; the interrupt plan (0x44D4E0 at goal 53's level) and the start of the run are the caller's, and a fidgeting critter's art set (0x43EB30) is not modelled (the viewer's hero never fidgets)

name: scenery loop starter
reason: Start covers the main-run refusal, the goal choice and the 5 ms first step for every loop; the art in slot 8 is not stored (the host draws from the object)

name: walk starter
reason: only its first step: the in-place retarget of a running walk (a new destination overwrites the bottom goal's destination and sets the replan path flag); the movement gate, the always-run conversion to the run starter, the build, the interrupt and the start are the starters' and the caller's, and the network branch is not followed

name: movement gate
reason: Original: The gate of the walk and run starters: the object must be active (0x45D790); in a round only the current participant passes; a PC then passes, an NPC only when it has no conversation partner (object field 0x129, read by 0x4C1110). Ours: The viewer's IAreaHeroRunsViewer.MayStart asks the hero's gate and AreaAiHost.StartGatePasses asks the round test only; the activity test and the NPC's conversation-partner test are not in the host's gate.

name: walk append starter
reason: AppendWalk does the found-run branch (insert at the bottom, same tile changes nothing, the full stack case) and answers NoRun so the caller starts a fresh walk; the always-run conversion and the network branch are left out

name: run starter
reason: Walk(run: true) does the gate, the in-place retarget, the new run after the level-3 interrupt and the flight mark of a held input; the encumbrance test for flag 0x40, the NPC callers and the network branch are not there

name: run append starter
reason: Original: The run form of the walk append for a runner by the always-run rule (the town map's further waypoints): a found run of goal 4 (or its aliases) gets run flag 0x40 always (its encumbrance test is dead code) and a goal 3 for the tile is appended unless the bottom goal already targets it; with no run a fresh goal 4 starts. Ours: Nearest is AreaHeroRunsHost.AppendWalk, which finds the walk run through aliases 7 and 4 and appends goal 3 but has no run-flag branch of its own.

name: move near tile starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 7 (the script's walk to and the route walk): movement gate, then a run of goal 4 (aliases 3, 7, 55) already walking gets its destination overwritten and the replan flag set (same tile changes nothing); otherwise goal 7 starts; a multiplayer client sends a packet. Ours: AreaAiHost.StartRouteWalk (a plain comment names the address) and AreaAiHost.ScriptWalk do the NPC form; the hero and the network path have none.

name: run near tile starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 55 for the script action 74: movement gate; a found walk gets run flag 0x40 when its owner's encumbrance is below 4 (even for the same tile), another tile retargets it in place; otherwise goal 55 starts, with the flag set on the new run. Ours: AreaAiHost.ScriptWalk (run: true) does the NPC form, including the encumbrance test; its documentation comment names GT158-GT161 and not this address.

name: follow starter
reason: the animation interrupt and the gate's facts are the world's; the join refresh (0x436FA0) is the party owner's

name: flee starter
reason: the run's set-up and the animation interrupt are the host's; the run flag 0x400 is the run's Flight flag

name: attack starter
reason: the throwable weapon's test and its removal, the interrupt, the step apart (0x4364D0) and the boomerang test are the world's; an attack run on another target is retargeted (inference)

name: get up starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 63: the start gate with cost 0, then, only when the critter's art shows animation 7, goal 63 with animation 8 through the level-3 interrupt; called by the fatigue recovery event, the heal and the script heal fatigue. Ours: AiExecutorRules.GetUpFrame builds the frame and GoalStarterKind keeps the gate; there is no one method of the starter, and AreaHeroKnockdown draws the hero's get-up.

name: knockback starter
reason: Start with KnockbackRules.Destination does the destination, the refusal at the map edge, the level-5 start and the run's tracking; the source object is not stored in the frame (slot 4)

name: throw starter
reason: the equal goal already queued (0x44E6F0) is read as an equal throw in the object's one run; the animation interrupt is the world's

name: dying starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 31 called only by the kill 0x45DA20: interrupts every run of the critter and starts the dying goal with the kill's animation. Ours: AiExecutorRules.DyingFrame builds the frame; the interrupt and the start belong to the life host, with no method of the starter's own.

name: skill starter
reason: the run's set-up: the frame's target, item and skill, run flag 0x4000 and running; the start gate; a missing target refuses (inference: the original asserts)

name: use item with skill starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 40 (script action 79 and the hero's lockpick or healing kit): the start gate with cost 4, then goal 40 with the target, item and skill, run flag 0x4000 and running when not encumbered. Ours: GameSessionOwner heals through GameSessionHeal for the hero; the AI host's StartSkillWithItem answers 'not ready' for an NPC.

name: item use starter
reason: the run's set-up: the frame's target and item, run flag 0x4000 and running for an NPC; the PC's always-run is the host's

name: use item on tile starter
reason: Original: Hero-only starter of goal 41 (trap device on a tile): the start gate with cost 4, then goal 41 with the tile and the item; sets no run flags. Ours: Goal 41 exists in GoalType and GoalDescriptors only; no starter or node runs it.

name: pickup starter
reason: the item system's switch (0x4681A0) is the world's fact

name: stun starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 57: refused unless the critter can act (alive, conscious, not stunned, paralysed or stoned); level-4 interrupt, then goal 57 with a countdown of (20 minus constitution) over 2. Ours: AiExecutorRules.StunFrame builds the frame with the countdown and LifeRules tests the gate; there is no one method of the starter.

name: projectile starter
reason: Launch with ProjectileRules.Flight starts the run (no gate, first step 5 ms later) and builds the flight line; the art and facing of the projectile are the viewer's

name: boomerang turn
reason: the new line from the tile being left to the thrower's tile and the returning flag; the flight goal's record writes (its target slot, start object, path flag) are the host's flight; the line's pixel start and the rest of the tick after the turn were not read

name: knock down starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 62: level-5 interrupt, then the knock-down goal with the fall animation; called by the damage path, the fatigue setter, the slip in the walk step and the spell component. Ours: AiExecutorRules.KnockDownFrame builds the frame; the interrupt level lives in GoalStarterKind.KnockDown; AreaHeroKnockdown draws the hero's fall.

name: become prone starter
reason: Original: Script action 93 for one object: level-4 interrupt (a refusal answers 0), then the art becomes animation 7 at its last frame; no goal, no flag. Ours: AreaAiHost.ScriptProne does it for an NPC of the shown map; its comment names the interrupt 0x424070 and GT187, not this address.

name: fidget starter
reason: FidgetAfterRun carries the tests (gate, no running animation, the art test, combat mode or auto-animate) and answers whether the fidget starts; the start itself is the host's

name: auto animation start
reason: Original: For a PC or NPC with critter flag 2 bit 0x2 (auto-animates) outside a round, starts the fidget (0x435BD0); always answers 1; called by the follower pass and the object list insert. Ours: FidgetAfterRun covers the fidget start; the auto-animation trigger after a leaderless NPC's routine is listed as not ready in AreaAiHost.RunRoutine.

name: unconceal starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 54 for an NPC that can act and has no main run, called by the magic object flag component when concealment ends: builds and starts the goal at its own priority. Ours: The unconceal run is only reached from goal nodes (world.Unconceal); no starter for the spell effect.

name: wander starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 65 for a wanderer at its standpoint: a PC or NPC that can act, in a round only the participant, radius above 0, no main run; a critter sharing the tile is asked to move (0x4363E0) and the start answers 0; otherwise goal 65 starts with the tether location and radius. Ours: NpcRouteRules marks the standpoint step with a wanderer as not implemented; no starter exists.

name: dark wander starter
reason: Original: Same starter as the wander starter for goal 66, the wander that seeks darkness, for NPC flag 0x2000. Ours: NpcRouteRules marks the standpoint step with a wanderer in the dark as not implemented; no starter exists.

name: pick locks starter
reason: the art test and the animation's loop count (frames and the expertise halving) are the world's; the frame flag 0x400 it sets is not modelled

name: please move starter
reason: Original: Starter of goal 68: when two critters share a tile, the one that is not a PC (the lower handle between two NPCs) is asked to step aside; start gate cost 0, refused for a busy one, then goal 68 with the other critter stored. Ours: No counterpart; AiExecutorRules calls a port StepApart that AreaAiHost leaves empty.

name: step apart request
reason: Original: When several living, not busy critters stand on one cell, one stays (a PC first) and each other NPC is asked to step away through the please move starter 0x4363E0; the follow request, the attack start's refusal and the leaderless routine call it. Ours: The port AiExecutorRules calls (StepApart) is an empty method in AreaAiHost, so nothing separates stacked critters.

name: tile sharer finder
reason: Original: Looks at the critters on the source's tile and, when more than one living, not busy critter shares it, answers the other NPC that blocks (the source and blocker out); called by the attack starter and both wander starters before they start or ask the blocker to move. Ours: No counterpart.

name: spread out starter
reason: the goal start only: the order that sets the NPC flag (0x45F600) is slice I9's

name: running flag setter
reason: Original: Sets run flag 0x40 (running) on a run by handle when its owner's encumbrance level is below 4; a multiplayer client sends a packet; nineteen call sites in seven functions. Ours: AiExecutorRules.ActionFlags (a plain comment names the address) sets running by the NPC's fatigue and the hero's walk by the always-run rule; the encumbrance test of this setter is modelled only inside AreaAiHost.ScriptWalk.

name: run flag setter
reason: TurnOnRunFlags ors the run flags of a run that is not being stepped and refuses a missing run; the path-flag word and the network branch are not there

name: animation speed refresh
reason: Original: Refreshes the speed of an object's running animation after a change that alters it (join, leave, wield, encumbrance level, effect add or remove): sets run flag 0x80 on its main run and marks its walk run to plan again. Ours: GameSessionOwner's encumbrance recalculation says the animation speed is the host's; no method refreshes it.

name: summoner source write
reason: Original: Called by the summon effect for an object without an inventory: writes the summoner's handle into frame slot 4 (the source object) of every goal run the new object owns. Ours: The summon component keeps the summoner as the created object's source for the burn (SessionSpellCaster summon, SUM4); no run slot is written.

name: weapon hit eye candy
reason: Original: Plays a weapon's own eye candy from the weapon eye-candy list (index of the prototype minus 6029 times 5 plus the kind) for a swing or hit event of its wielder (or of a weapon object itself), queueing a second one for kind 3; answers non-zero when it ran, and at the hit in the attack end that answer vetoes the damage effect. Ours: No counterpart; the weapon's own hit effect and its veto of the damage effect are not modelled.

name: animation frame rate
reason: Original: Frames per second of a critter's animation: for critter arts of body 1 or 2 the walk and run rates gain 4; per weapon slot and animation a low, middle and high value scaled by speed; art rate for other arts, the throw and elemental bodies. Ours: RealTimeCombatRules.AttackFramesPerSecond does the attack tables (its comment names ARC-RENDER-039, not the address) and HeroBody.GaitRateBonus the walk and run offset; no one method.

name: wall check update ping
reason: Original: Per-frame module ping: when a recalculation is pending, recalculates the roof of the stored tile (0x439D30) and then the wall fade (0x437E50) and clears the pending flag. Ours: The viewer recalculates through AreaWallCheck.Recalculate and AreaRoofGrid on hero moves; no ping or pending flag.

name: wall check recalculation
reason: Original: Recalculates which walls in front of the player fade: resolves the player's tile to its 4x4 block, walks the ordered lattice edges, adds or releases walls in the check (0x438570, 0x438830) and roof fades; skipped when the wall check option is off. Ours: AreaWallCheck.Recalculate does the block resolve and edge walk (the class comment names 0x437E50, the method's does not); the option switch is not there.

name: wall check add wall
reason: Original: Adds a wall to the sorted held-wall array with its fade mode (left, right or both by its rotation), its normalised roof tile and its sector lock, and counts its roof (0x438720). Ours: The viewer loop in TerrainViewerAreaRoofs joins walls through AreaRoofGrid.AddWallFade; the held array and the sector lock are not modelled.

name: wall check apply
reason: Original: Applies the held walls' pending state: a wall marked for release loses its fade bits, is redrawn, uncounts its roof (0x438A50), unlocks its sector (0x4D0AE0) and leaves the array; a wall marked new gets its left, right or both fade bits. Ours: AreaWallCheck.Reset and AreaRoofGrid.ReleaseWallFade release the fade and roof; the sector unlock and the per-wall flag bits are the renderer's.

name: roof draw
reason: only the corner alphas of a faded piece; the drawing itself (outdoor colour and blit) is the renderer's

name: roof hit test
reason: only the roof of the tile under the point moved 120 down; the screen location and the opaque-pixel test are the renderer's

name: roof fade on
reason: on a tile without a roof the original still writes the empty slot back and marks the sector as having a roof list; that write and the rectangle invalidation are not modelled

name: roof faded test
reason: the debug roof toggle is not modelled (roofs are always on)

name: roof cover test
reason: the debug roof toggle is not modelled and the caller tells whether the tile is indoor

name: roof fill flood
reason: the screen rectangle it invalidates is the renderer's; the flood is iterative where the original recurses (same end state)

name: object draw list builder
reason: only the decision to skip the body of a dont-draw or invisible object (overlays are drawn either way); the lists, lights, sorting and the rest of the builder are the scene plan and the canvas

name: hovered object set
reason: the AREA viewer keeps the hovered object of its own pick and highlights a portal, container, scenery or item (AreaHoverWindow.Highlighted, ARC-UI-057, OH2); the critter rings (arts 467, 468, 555 in combat mode) and their reaction colours are not built

name: highlighted object get
reason: only the attack order use: the viewer key becomes a session combatant on the shown map, none when it is not one; the highlight state itself (set 0x43C270, clear 0x43C4A0) is the viewer hover, not a method

name: hovered ring under
reason: the critter ring under the objects (art 467 or 555, OH4) is not built

name: hovered object draw over
reason: the AREA viewer draws the hovered portal, container, scenery or item a second time, additive with its source tinted by (200, 200, 200), unlit, after the bodies and before the roofs (TerrainCanvas.AreaHighlight, ARC-UI-057, OH3); the detect-invisible exception, the wading split and the critter ring over the objects are not built

name: object create from prototype
reason: CreateProjectile and CreateMissile (GameSessionOwner) create the session entity of a projectile or a spell missile on the active map; prototype building, the dynamic flag, sector listing, notification and the other kinds of creation (items, pools, traps, summons) are not carried by them

name: object destroy
reason: a script's destroy (68, TD2) of an NPC of the shown map is the AREA viewer's map change obj.destroyed, which hides the NPC from the view, the object lists and the AI; the destroy event (point 2) is not run (an NPC with a destroy script is refused), nor the clean-up, the contents or the network path; the PC and a follower of the PC are refused (ARC-SCRIPT-052)

name: object leaves sector list
reason: Original: Detaches the lights and render state of an object, finds its sector and, when the object is static or the sector is loaded, removes it from that sector object list with the sector locked. Ours: No method; residency moves and evicts entities as whole sets (the sector and map hosts, GameSessionOwner.DestroyObject for the destroy), nothing removes one object from a list.

name: object teardown and free
reason: Original: Removes the speech bubble and floater, kills every goal run of the object (0x423FF0), ends its spells (0x459740), removes its AI events (0x4AD7D0), runs the destroyed hook, detaches lights and render state and frees the object record; used by map clear and the editor. Ours: GameSessionOwner.DestroyObject covers the run, spell and AI event part of the one destroy path; the free of the record at map clear has no counterpart (our entities are dropped with the map host).

name: object flag set
reason: Original: Sets object flag bits with their side effects: turning OFF on removes the speech bubble, floater and lights, a few bits (0x80000, 0x10000000, 0x20000000, 0x100000) mark the render cache stale, bit 0x4 first runs a render state update, then the old and new rectangles are redrawn. Ours: No method; the session writes the flag state per feature (ScrObjectStateChange toggle off, ObjectLights.FlagsAtLoad for the light off bit of the clear 0x43D280); the bubble, floater and light removal side effects are the viewer's.

name: object flags clear
reason: only that clearing OF_OFF clears the object's lights' OFF bit (a nocturnal light switched on at load)

name: item damage setter
reason: only the write of a negative value as 0; the network client branch, the critter rest timer and the change notification are not an item rule

name: critter resistance
reason: a critter's resistances with the resistance effects (after armour and the poison bonus, before the clamp; ARC-MAGIC-027) and without the display form that leaves out unidentified magickal armour; the magic type is no result of the combat function

name: armour class
reason: only the worn items part on the attack path (unidentified magickal items are not modelled); the base value, effects and the adjustment stat are in the attack rules

name: object type is sector type
reason: Original: True for the sector types wall (0), portal (1), scenery (3) and trap (17); containers, projectiles, items, PCs and NPCs are false. Decides which objects the sector files own. Ours: No such predicate; a map rows are one immutable list of T0 records and changes are session records per feature (the document row RL1 states this).

name: object is static
reason: Original: True for a sector type object (wall, portal, scenery, trap) without OF_DYNAMIC (0x2000); the flush skips static objects (their changes go to the sector differences), the create path and the ID getter branch on it. Ours: No such predicate; static versus mobile is which file a record came from (Arcanum.Data StaticObjects versus the mobile records) plus session records per feature.

name: screen object pick
reason: the AREA viewer picks the frontmost opaque body and skips OF_CLICK_THROUGH (AreaHoverIndex.Pick, ARC-UI-005, OH1); the editor switch, the type table and the pick fallbacks are not modelled

name: object screen rectangle
reason: only the restock caller: whether the container body meets the game window, with the rectangle taken from the viewer draw plan instead of computed; the rectangle itself, the type cases and the error are not carried

name: object move to location
reason: only a projectile or a spell missile (MoveProjectile, MoveMissile): cell and pixel offsets of the session entity; sector lists, lights, redraw and the notification (tile script, jump point) are not done by it; other moves (followers, drops) are their own host steps

name: teleported event callback
reason: Original: The callback of the Teleported event (data slot 0x5B2728): for a non-null object handle runs the location change notification 0x444270 with mode 2 (jump point and tile script of the tile it stands on) and answers 1. Ours: SessionTeleportedMark keeps the mark and the viewer TakeTeleportedMarks runs the notice after the map opens; no method of Session, World or Simulation carries the callback.

name: object offset set if alive
reason: Original: Writes the pixel offsets (fields 3 and 4) of a not destroyed object through the offset apply 0x4423E0; the hover goal raises and bobs the object this way. Ours: AreaEyeCandyHost.HoverShift keeps the hover raise in the host own table (HoverOffset) added to the draw, not in the object offset fields; the interface member it implements carries the address in its comment.

name: object art set
reason: Original: Sets the current art (field 1) of a not destroyed object, clears its render cache bit, redraws the old and new rectangles and restarts the scenery animation (0x43F710); 139 callers (facing turns, wield changes, goals). Ours: No method; the session keeps art and facing as per feature records and the hosts apply them (turn, wield, scenery loop restart in SceneryAnimationRules.Restart).

name: object primary light set
reason: Original: Writes the primary light fields (13 art, 14 colour, 15 flags) of an object (stopping the old light animation when the art becomes -1), clears the render bit and rebuilds the object lights (0x4D9590). Ours: CarriedLightRules (Data.Lighting) holds the carried light colours and art; nothing applies a light to an object like this one (the viewer draws lights from its own build).

name: object overlay slot set
reason: Original: Writes one entry of an object overlay list (foreground field 6, background field 7 or underlay field 8) and recomputes the object flags 0x8000 (has foreground or background parts) and 0x10000 (has underlays); redraws the object. Ours: The overlays are shown from the eye candy run state (AreaEyeCandyHost.Shown, AiExecutorRules.EyeCandyNode); no object field is written and the two flags are not kept.

name: object light slot set
reason: Original: Writes the art, colour and flags of one overlay light slot (fields 16, 17, 18) of an object (stopping the old light animation for art -1), clears the render bit and rebuilds the object lights. Ours: Not modelled; the eye candy runs carry the light parts as data only (SpellEyeCandyEntry), no light is built on the object.

name: object break
reason: the item branch (types 5..14): the destroyed bits, the damage reset and the second-break deletion; the portal, container, scenery and trap branches are ObjectDamageRules.Break (ARC-COMBAT-008, ledger OD7–OD11); taking the item off or dropping it, the BUST script and the animation stop are the caller's, the busting and destroying sounds are played by the viewer (SoundCueRules.Misc; ARC-RENDER-1126); walls (never reached by an attack) are not implemented

name: scenery respawn event
reason: the scenery is switched on again (the session clears its off condition); the flag words and the redraw are the host's

name: object busted test
reason: Original: Answers whether a non-critter is busted: 0 for a destroyed object; a portal or container by its busted bit (0x80), scenery by bit 0x2 of its flags, a trap by bit 0x2 of its trap flags, a wall by its art being broken, 0 for other types. Ours: Spread over SessionObjectFacts.FromCombatFields (busted flag of breakable scenery and traps), LockRules (BustedBit for portals and containers) and the hostility facts Busted flag; no one method answers it, and the wall case is not read.

name: scenery animation start
reason: the drawn case at load (visible scenery, no scenery flag 0x1, not stoned, more than one frame); the sound-only loop and stopping runs are not modelled, nor its runtime callers (OFF cleared, ART set)

name: object frame step
reason: the next frame (wrapping to 0); the offset move by the frame delta is SceneryLoop.Advance's and the redraw the viewer's

name: container previous frame
reason: Original: The close of a container or portal: steps the art one frame back (frame 0 stays), shifts the pixel offsets by the new frame delta when it has one, clears the render bit and redraws; a destroyed object is skipped. Ours: No method; the session keeps the open state, the viewer draws the container frames (the next-frame twin 0x43F7F0 is SceneryAnimationRules partial).

name: overlay art next frame
reason: Original: Advances the art of one overlay list entry (field and index given) to its next frame (wrapping), clears the render bit and redraws; the eye candy animation update uses it. Ours: The frame is the run state EyeCandy.Frame in the goal frame (AiExecutorRules.EyeCandyFrameStep); no art is written into an object slot.

name: overlay art previous frame
reason: Original: Steps the art of one overlay list entry back one frame (to the given wrap frame when it has none before), clears the render bit and redraws; the reversed eye candy plays use it. Ours: As the next frame twin: the reverse frame is the run state in AiExecutorRules.EyeCandyFrameStep, no object slot is written.

name: overlay light art first frame
reason: Original: Sets the overlay light art (field 17, given index) to its first frame, clears the render bit and rebuilds the object lights; begin node of a forward eye candy play. Ours: Not modelled; the light part of an eye candy entry is data only.

name: overlay light art last frame
reason: Original: Sets the overlay light art (field 17, given index) to its last frame when it is not there, clears the render bit and rebuilds the object lights; begin node of a reversed eye candy play. Ours: Not modelled; the light part of an eye candy entry is data only.

name: path step object traversal
reason: Original: The object traversal of one path step in the request mode: calls the step cost 0x43FDC0 with out values and answers blocked when it costs or when the step crosses a window piece; the path request, the knockback block test and others call it. Ours: AreaDropMap.Traverse answers it for the drop mode (comment only, private) and IOriginalPathMap.Traverse is the interface the path request reads; no public method carries the address, and the other modes (path request, knockback) use their own step tests.

name: step cost
reason: only the projectile flags 0x0C without a mover (the line of fire's step); the sound flag 0x20 is priced by the sound cost's step (AwarenessRules.SoundStepCost) and the walking mode is the step evidence's

name: walker door test
reason: answers only the closed idle door of a neighbour step from the route snapshot; the step-cost call with its flags and the mode argument are not reproduced; the twin entry at 0x440760 (flags 6, no callers) is dead

name: objects at tile list
reason: only the spell host answers this query; the other 77 callers (path, traversal, destroy, junk piles) use their own lookups; sector lock accounting, list order and the live-sector requirement are not modelled

name: objects in rectangle list
reason: ours takes a square around a centre (spell area), not an arbitrary rectangle; the other callers (AI target search, vicinity) use their own lookups; sector locks and list order are not modelled

name: vicinity list
reason: script focus 8 and 9 only (PCs and NPCs, plus scenery in a sibling method): a fixed 10-tile square on both axes instead of the window rectangle converted by 0x4B9130; the trap shooter, experience, spell pick and the other eight callers have no equivalent; list order unread

name: direct followers list
reason: Original: Builds a list of the handles in an object follower array (field 241) in array order, one node each. Ours: no list-building counterpart: the session keeps only the PC follower array as party state and every caller reads it directly; NPC leaders have no follower array

name: all followers list
reason: answers only for the PC (the session party followers that the world knows); no followers of followers and an NPC leader gets an empty list; the order is the array order only

name: team list
reason: Original: For a PC (type 15) builds its party list and appends each member own recursive follower list; any other object gives a list with only itself; used for the enemy team add, the spell target collection and 0x44B4E0. Ours: no shared function: the enemy team add and the spell pick each build hero plus follower array themselves, without followers of followers

name: object place in world
reason: Original: Puts an object on the map at a location: clears the held flag, writes the location, zeroes the offsets, lists it in its loaded sector, relights it, runs the location notification (tile script for critters), redraws. Ours: no shared function: our session lays an item on a cell inside each caller (drop, spill, throw, junk pile settle) without the sector list, light, tile-script or redraw steps

name: object take into holder
reason: Original: Takes an object off the map into a holder: frees its lights, unlists it from its sector when loaded, sets the held flag, writes the parent field with the holder handle and redraws; a network client asks the host first. Ours: no method of ours carries it: the session moves the item from its placed-item records into the hero list with insert checks; sector list, lights, held flag, parent field, redraw and the lock request are not modelled; the same step of the other callers (barter, 0x464470, 0x49D690) has no separate counterpart

name: object script run
reason: no single dispatcher: the use point runs in AreaUseScriptHost (the PC's use in Run, an arbitrary triggerer in RunUseScript, ARC-MAGIC-048), other points in per-point hosts (dying, damage, bust, examine, heartbeat, item); points 2, 3, 6, 7 and 8 are not hosted; the whole-slot overwrite is an explicit writeback record applied by the host

name: object display name
reason: a PC player name is not resolved (PlayerNameNotModelled) and the editor flag that shows every item name is not modelled; the output buffer copy is replaced by a typed result

name: race and gender set
reason: only the body type and gender of the drawn art (with the elf woman using the human body); the stat writes with their innate effects live in the session hero definition and field 0x21 is not modelled; NPC prototypes carry their own art

name: lockable object test
reason: Original: True for a portal or a container except the junk pile (the prototype whose number is 3023), false for anything else; the lock, jam and locked-get functions return 0 for non-lockable objects. Ours: no lockable predicate: lock rules take flags only and the hosts apply them to portals and containers; a junk pile in ours carries no lock state

name: lock event
reason: only the flags; the session closes the object (GameSessionOwner.FireLockReset)

name: fold first tick
reason: an immediate AI tick 1 ms ahead for a resident NPC that is not destroyed, on the open map only; the editor-flag guard is not modelled; inside an event pass the tick waits for the pass end

name: object create tail
reason: Original: Creates an object from a prototype (with a requested id when the id word is not -1) and finishes it with 0x442260; it is the tail of both create entries 0x43CBA0 and 0x43CBF0. Ours: no general creation path: the session creates only projectiles, missiles, junk piles and made items through their own hosts, without dynamic flag, sector listing or the finish steps

name: object copy tail
reason: Original: Copies an object (with a given id or a new one), finishes it with 0x442260, moves the copy to its location and, for an NPC, sets both standpoint fields (0x121, 0x122) to that location. Ours: no object copy in ours; the callers 0x43CC30 and 0x43CC70 have no counterpart

name: object create finish
reason: Original: Finishes a created object: marks it and its inventory items dynamic (flag 0x2000), lists it in its loaded sector, relights it, delays an AI tick for an NPC, runs restock, the location notification (mode 2), redraws. Ours: ours has no dynamic flag, no sector listing, no creation-time AI tick or restock: new objects are added by their own hosts; saved dynamic objects are a different schema

name: object offset apply
reason: Original: Applies new sub-tile offsets (fields 3 and 4) to an object: updates its per-tile registrations (0x4D6210, 0x4D5570, not read further), re-sorts it in its sector list, runs the location notification in mode 0 (no tile script), moves its lights. Ours: ours keeps no per-object pixel offsets: movement is whole tiles with presentation interpolation, so no frame offset writes or offset re-sort exist

name: object blit setup
reason: only the constant alpha 0x80 of a translucent or invisible object (when no blit mode of its own is set); the colour modes, wading and palette parts are the scene plan

name: object frame rectangle
reason: only the shrunk half (frame width, height and hotspot shifted right by one) of the rectangle; the scale percent part is the scene plan

name: object location change notification
reason: jump point and tile script for the player and tile script for an NPC (AreaMapTransfers.Enter, EnterByCritter) and the sector script on entry are covered; not covered here: the wading flag recomputed on every move, the party follower callback, redraw (viewer)

name: burning scenery on tile
reason: Original: Lists the scenery on a tile and returns the first object that has a running fire goal (75 or 77); the path search adds 80 to a tile with fire when the mover carries walk flag 0x400. Ours: No fire probe and no walk flags 0x200 and 0x400 in OriginalPathRequest: a path never avoids burning scenery or scales cost by light as the original does (LR9)

name: alt click pull object onto hero tile
reason: Original: Alt click on a PC, NPC or loose item (types 5 to 14, not in inventory) within one tile of the hero relocates it to the hero tile by the ordinary move 0x43E770; farther away it refuses through a UI hook. Ours: No counterpart: HeroClickRules names the Alt action as not read; nothing relocates an adjacent object onto the hero tile; whether the original gates it by a cheat mode was not read (caller 0x54ED30 game view mouse input)

name: script run entry
reason: network host gate not applicable; dialog point with call script refused; run limits are project options; a missing script file or a trap script returns skip default as in the original

name: global variable get
reason: original has no index bounds test; ours stops the run on an index outside 0..1999 by owner rule (undefined read not reproduced)

name: global variable set
reason: original has no index bounds test and sends a network message in multiplayer; ours stops on an index outside 0..1999

name: global flag get
reason: original has no index bounds test; ours stops the run on an index outside the flag range

name: global flag set
reason: spill reproduced by the GlobalFlagWriteSpills rule; no index bounds test in the original, ours stops on an index outside the range; multiplayer send not applicable

name: story state set
reason: single player: the network message is not sent

name: script time event callback
reason: ours may refuse a call and report false (no script host on the map), the original always returns 1 after the dispatcher validated the handles

name: script condition
reason: the five guard conditions of conditional map transitions only (SG1–SG6: PC quest state, holds an item named, is named, wields an item named, has a reputation) over one object each; focus groups are not admitted, and an absent object stops the run where the original takes the false branch; the other conditions are the dispatcher's earlier slices, not migrated to the registry yet; the identified (47, WE5) and items-being-rewielded (50, WE6) conditions are the interpreter's, answered by the host (ARC-SCRIPT-042); the obj-is-dead (22, HW1) and obj-is-switched-off (27, HW2) conditions are the interpreter's list rule (SG6) over the host's answers, single objects only (ARC-SCRIPT-049); the spell conditions obj-has-body-spell (14, SC1), obj-is-influenced-by-spell (35, SC2), knows-spell (48, SC3) and mastered-spell-college (49, SC4) are the interpreter's list rule over the host's answers (`IScrSpellQueries`, ARC-MAGIC-029; no host answers yet)

name: script action
reason: the teleport (44) and fade-and-teleport (102) cases (TR1, TR2): the request goes to the host, which owns the pending-teleport rule (TR4), the fade, the time advance, the sound and the movie; an absent object asks for nothing; the set-auto-level-scheme case (139, OL30) is the interpreter's one request per object of its operand (one method per address); the show-book, show-picture and show-plaque cases (64, 65, 114, WR rows) are the interpreter's one request for their number and viewer, which the viewer shows to the PC only; the start-schematic-UI case (129, SW8, NC3, TC2 both fixed) is the interpreter's one request for its operand, which the viewer resolves (a PC opens its window, an NPC with a PC leader opens it as the crafter); the get-skill case (47, SX1, SX2) is the interpreter's store of the host's effective level (0 outside 0..15, an absent object stops the run), and the use-item-with-skill case (79, SX3) the interpreter's one request for its five operands, which no host runs yet (ledger section script-skill-commands-arc-skills-009); the assign-object (15) and get-object-type (34) cases (OV2, OV3) are the interpreter's, single objects only, an absent object stopping the run where the original reads undefined values; the call-script case (7) is 0x44B030; the other cases are the dispatcher's earlier slices, not migrated to the registry yet; the add-effect, remove-effect, magick-tech adjustment and play-script-eye-candy cases (77, 78, 91, 120; WE1, WE2, WE4) are the interpreter's requests and store, and call-ex (81, WE3) its nested run (ARC-SCRIPT-042); the random (37, PG5), loop-for and loop-end (18, 19, PG7) and create-object (52, PG1) cases are the interpreter's draw from the host's generator, its run loop and its one request for the prototype number and the object, whose tile the session draws (DropPlacementRules.PlaceCreated: ten tries of a distance 1..3 and the placement 0x4F4E40) and whose object is an item of the ground store only (ARC-WORLD-081); the distance-between case (71, HW3) is the interpreter's store of the tile distance of the host's two places (an absent object or place stops the run), and set faction (134, HW4) its one request for the first object, which the viewer applies to an NPC only (ARC-SCRIPT-049); destroy (68, TD1) and stop attacking (109, TD3) are its one request for the first object, which the viewer applies from tile and sector scripts (ARC-SCRIPT-052); the get-stat case (33, GS1–GS4) is the interpreter's store of the host's effective stat, intelligence above 4 read as 1 for a dumb background, an absent object stopping the run and a stat the host cannot answer ending the dispatch as not modelled (ARC-DEV-157); the get-reaction case (29, GR1) is the interpreter's store of the host's standard effective reaction of the first object of operand 0 toward the first of operand 1, an absent object stopping the run and a pair the host cannot answer ending the dispatch as not modelled (ARC-DEV-178); the unfog-town-map case (113, UF1) hands a positive town-map number to the host, 0 and negative numbers asking for nothing (ARC-DEV-205); the give-spell-mastery case (112, SC5) hands the first object and the college as read to the host (ARC-MAGIC-029)

name: remove script call predicate
reason: removes the first matching pending call only; the original remover 0x45BFF0 also takes one match from the side list kept during a ping, which the session has no counterpart for

name: call script
reason: one call for the single objects of operands 2 and 3 (the original runs every triggerer and attachee pair of two groups, sharing one copy of the callee's header); the callee's own header flags and counters, fresh variables, no extra object, its changes to itself discarded and its return code ignored (OV1); a missing callee, a trap script and a monster-generator attachee run nothing; a refused callee or one with a dialog action refuses the whole dispatch, an unreadable one or a nesting or line count beyond the project bounds ends it (the original recurses until its stack runs out); the dialog-point gates (E6) are not applied to a callee

name: call script ex
reason: one object of operand 0 and one triggerer (the set's single focus kinds); a use or dialog point, a dialog action in the callee and a trap object whose script becomes 0 refuse the dispatch; a point outside 0..35 or the dialog-override slot ends it; nesting and lines share the call bounds (ARC-SCRIPT-018)

name: float line
reason: the dialog PC from the host's critters around the triggerer and one request per object; no triggerer floats nothing (not traced in the original); the host shows the text of a plain DLG line (a separators-only action field counts as empty) and leaves the run unapplied for a line with an action field or generated text; the original's speech display (0x568540) is not modelled, the viewer floats the text in the floater field

name: print line
reason: the shown text of a plain DLG line; a line with an action field (other than separators only, ARC-SCRIPT-050) or generated text is refused, not run; the second number goes to the host unread; the network path is not modelled; the original's skipped cache release (IS3) has no counterpart

name: script focus object list
reason: only triggerer, attachee, extra, player, local object, looped object and the vicinity kinds 8, 9 and 15 are modelled; followers, party, team, group and the container, portal and item vicinity kinds are not admitted

name: first object of an operand
reason: Only the focus kinds of the admission set are resolved (triggerer, attachee, extra, player, object variable, looped object, the three vicinity kinds); follower, party, team, group and inventory list kinds are refused at admission; an empty list reads as no object where the original reads an uninitialised slot (SU8, deliberate).

name: write object operand
reason: The assign-object action covers triggerer, attachee, extra object and object variable; a write to the current looped object (focus kind 10) is ignored where the original stores it.

name: read number operand
reason: A value kind above 6 answers the operand itself in the original; ours refuses such a kind at admission (project strictness).

name: write number operand
reason: A literal or a kind above 6 is ignored by the original; ours refuses such a store at admission.

name: load script header into slot
reason: Serves the map patch's script lines only; the other callers (call script, 0x445140, 0x411940, 0x468930) take the header from the parsed program (ScrProgram), which carries the same two words.

name: script body read
reason: Ours also refuses a file whose length is not exactly header plus lines, a negative count or a capacity below the count; the original reads what it finds and accepts trailing bytes.

name: script eye candy add
reason: Original: Starts entry N of the script eye-candy list on an object (the add 0x4CCF70: goals 45-48, 58, 59, 75, 76 by the entry's flags, or a static overlay, no interrupt; a null or destroyed object is refused); also used by exploding weapons with entry 55. Ours: Our script interpreter only records (number, object) in ScrEffects.EyeCandies; no host loads ScriptEyeCandy.mes or starts the eye-candy run, and the exploding-weapon effect is left to the host.

name: script eye candy remove
reason: Original: Removes the eye candy of the script list from an object (the remove 0x4CD940 over the object), reached from script action 124. Ours: Action 124 (stop script eye candy) is not in the interpreter's set; nothing removes a script eye candy.

name: count a significant goal
reason: the count is derived from the table's runs (SignificantGoalCount) instead of kept as a counter at the pushes; the method is the predicate both counting functions share

name: uncount a significant goal
reason: the count is derived from the table's runs (SignificantGoalCount) instead of kept as a counter at the free; the method is the predicate both counting functions share

name: restart a carried run
reason: Original: Restarts a run restored from a file or packet: clears its done mark, resets its stack top when empty, removes its pending animation events and queues one animation event at the saved time; callers are the map's Anim.dat loader 0x4230A0 and network code. Ours: Ours does not carry goal runs across maps (GS10) and rebuilds no animation event for a restored run; no counterpart of the restart.

name: run slot allocator
reason: the slot's work area and path block are not modelled, the run id counter starts at 1 where the original seeds it randomly, and the start's own steps (the owner copy, the first frame's event) are the caller's

name: run slot free
reason: the hero's attack target in the interface and the run's events are the caller's; the round's callback is called by the session after every free that leaves no significant goal (ARC-DEV-136: GameSessionOwner.AnimationsDone; the result carries the significant-goal count after the free)

name: runs of an object
reason: the next-run walk (0x44D340) is the order of the result; the table keeps no empty run

name: goal frame set-up
reason: Only the interrupt level of a generic start; the frame itself is the GoalFrame record's construction and the interrupt is run by GoalStartRules.Start.

name: run start
reason: the interrupts and refusals of the starters around it (gate, duplicate, interrupt levels, loading, destroyed object, full table) as pure rules, and the first frame's event 5 ms ahead on the animation clock, 1 ms for an owner that is not the current participant of a round (ARC-DEV-132, ARC-DEV-136: the session's StartGoal queues it); the hero's attack target in the interface, the network branch and the global 0x5E3508 refusal (meaning unread, Q4) are not modelled

name: goal queue insertion
reason: the queue of a cast beneath the caster's playing casting goal: the depth and turn-based refusals of the run start's goal branch (0x455C30) and the run freed on a refusal; the goal stack itself, its bottom insertion and the order of play are the viewer's for the hero and the AI host's for an NPC (ARC-WORLD-104, AC5); since ARC-DEV-131 the pure bottom insertion exists as GoalRunTable.InsertAtBottom, which nothing calls yet and which no row marks (one method per address); no subgoals are modelled, so the depth is the number of queued casts

name: run parameter set-up
reason: Original: Before a node step: refreshes the frame's five object parameters (a stale handle is re-found through the locator, failure asserts and answers false), sets the run owner, then copies the node's parameter indices into the working array (objects, locations, values, and four derived slots). Ours: Ours has typed frames per goal and no generic node-parameter loader; a stale object parameter's re-find and its failure answer are not reproduced.

name: stop attack goals at a head
reason: Original: Peace helper: when the object's main run has bottom goal 18 or 19 and its target is the head or a critter led by the head, the run is interrupted at level 5. Ours: The session reports Head and Followers in SessionPeaceStep but no host interrupts the NPC's attack run; only the stop-attacking priority-3 interrupt of the follower (AreaAiHost.ApplyStop) is applied.

name: stop attack goals at an enemy
reason: Original: Peace helper: when a follower's main run has bottom goal 18 or 19 and its target is exactly the given NPC, the run is interrupted at level 5. Ours: Same as 0x44E050: the follower list is reported by the session but no host interrupts the follower's attack run.

name: kill one run
reason: the events and end nodes of the killed run are the caller's

name: run interrupt rule
reason: the events and end nodes of the ended run are the caller's; the network branch is not followed; the table keeps no empty run

name: interrupt runs by goal
reason: the hold's call only (the ObjFlag component for goals 3 and 61 with the author -1, level 6): the runs whose bottom or current frame has the goal; the hosts interrupt them with their end nodes (ARC-DEV-302)

name: run with a bottom goal
reason: only the search from the object's first run; the search after a given run (its first candidate is not filtered by owner or use) is not modelled

name: equal goal queued
reason: the original compares five object parameters; the typed frame holds the target and the item (the owner is the run's own); the starters ask through the forwarder 0x44E6F0, which calls it with no out-handle, and this method serves both forms

name: first run attacks
reason: the party-wide branch (a player-character target matches when the run's target is one of its group) is not modelled; the leader function is the caller's

name: town map path check
reason: Original: The path search of the town map's waypoint adding: with request flag 1 and a search limit of 200, answers whether the PC can walk from the start location to the target; null or invalid locations answer false. Ours: no method of ours carries it: Method is in tools/terrain-viewer; ours bounds start and target to under 32 tiles apart and takes the route planner's first plan with no retry, where the original uses its own 64-by-64 window and limit.

name: magic tech init
reason: only the component type names and the spell text and record files with their order and failures; the eye-candy file and the run slots are not read, and a file the MES grammar refuses is refused (project policy)

name: spell runs at hero teleport
reason: Original: At a hero teleport to another map, each active spell run whose source, parent, target and summoned list all travel is written to the destination map's carry file and freed; any other run is ended forcibly. Ours: the runs that do not travel end through the forced end (Arcanum.Simulation.Magic.SpellRunTravelRules, SessionSpellCaster.EndRunsLeavingMap); the runs that travel stay in the session's one table (no carry file; the tick keeps its deadline, the first list at +0x130 is not tested).

name: spell runs parked at map close
reason: Original: At map close during a teleport, every spell run still active is written to the left map's carry file with no travel test and no free. Ours: not modelled (ARC-MAGIC-058): the session's run table is global, so the run a forced end leaves for a pending END callback simply stays in it.

name: spell runs restored at map entry
reason: Original: At map entry reads the map's carry file of spell runs; each record takes its own slot (or a new one), is copied in and has its next tick event queued again. Ours: not modelled (ARC-MAGIC-058): a carried run never left the global table and keeps its tick event with its old deadline; a save restores runs through the snapshot.

name: spell record load first pass
reason: the file is loaded by the magic tech init row; a refused line stops the read with a typed refusal where the original exits or crashes

name: spell record load first pass body
reason: Mid-function body of the first pass 0x44FE30 after the file opens (the export split it off): clears the component slots, reads records 0 to 79 at the message base, 80 to 139 with willpower minimum 0 and 140 to 222 at the base plus 2000 with the technology flag. Ours matches the record ranges and differs only in the typed refusal where the original exits on a failed open or line.

name: spell record read
reason: the record name (message n of the spell text file) is read by the spell texts

name: minimum intelligence to cast
reason: the constant 5 is SpellBookRules.MinimumIntelligence; the mark sits on the spellbook method that applies it (the cast check in SpellRunRules uses the same constant)

name: spell willpower minimum
reason: only the rank default before the spell table loads; a spell's own value comes from the data (AutoLevelTables.ReadSpellWillpower), and no installed record has one

name: spell payment
reason: single player only (the network message of a client is not modelled); the plan is applied by the run and the host (fields, recharge events, the AI notification and the interface refresh), and a spell number outside the table is refused at once where the original reads past it on its critter path; the cell branch asks the charge-cell port (ChargeCellRules, ARC-TECHNOLOGY-007), which answers an unapplied request without writing where the original takes the cells (CCA1)

name: spell run time cost
reason: the cost only: the payment it calls is its own row (0x450420), and a missing source (which returns success without paying) is the caller's

name: spell check cost
reason: the cost only: the payment it asks is its own row (0x450420), and a missing source (which logs and fails) is the caller's

name: spell pre animation check
reason: the cost only: finding the run by its slot is the run's (MT9a) and the payment it asks is its own row (0x450420)

name: spell parent of an object
reason: Original: Gives the parent a spell run uses for an object: none for none; a critter or any non-item itself; an item (types 5-14) in an inventory its holder (field 0x58), else the item itself. Ours: no method of ours carries it: The rule is inline in the item-spell starter (holder, else the item itself); there is no stand-alone getter and no critter/non-item case since only items are asked.

name: maintained run count
reason: Steamwoven counts the runs holding the critter's slots where the original answers 0 (MG11)

name: summon effect
reason: Original: Creates one object from a prototype id at a location (single player), flags it summoned (0x4000), then per type: scenery records the summoner as burn source; an NPC gets art, palette, faction, no experience, the summoner's alignment, OF_DONTDRAW and no pickpocket. Ours: ARC-MAGIC-053 (E1-e): the NPC half builds the created critter by the creation rule with the summoned flags, OF_DONTDRAW (shown at the animation callback), OCF2_NO_PICKPOCKET, experience cleared and the hero's alignment copied; not built: Clear_Faction:, Palette:, the concealed start (SUM19), the faction and alignment of an NPC summoner (E1-f).

name: spell run process entry
reason: the original logs a refused re-entry; here it is a host note; Steamwoven defers the refused run until after the pass (MG30, MagicAnomalyProfile.ReEntryDropsRuns)

name: spell run processing
reason: the network client's early exit is not modelled; the per-target stage (0x455550) and the resistance are the rules' (ARC-MAGIC-011); the component gate and the components are the host's ports; the target type cache is not kept; Steamwoven restores the source after a resisted target too (MG34, MagicAnomalyProfile.ResistedReflectionKeepsSwap)

name: agoal component
reason: Only goals 43 and 44 are done (the run itself is the host's); goals 24 and 62 and other animation goals are not started.

name: agoal terminate component
reason: Only the hover goal (44) is ended; other goal types are not interrupted.

name: ai redirect component
reason: Original: Redirects the target's neighbours' AI against the target: the component's MinIQ and critter-flag mask feed 0x4A9530/0x4A9560, which give each candidate an attack event and focus on the target. Ours: The redirect rule itself exists (Arcanum.Simulation.Ai.AiGroundRules) but the spell host never calls it; the component is logged not ready.

name: cast component
reason: ARC-MAGIC-049 (NC1–NC3): the invocation as the original builds it (no source, the run's parent, the current target object and tile, the parent's location as the source location, goal 73); the run starts after the outer action or event pass, not inside the component, and a chain is bounded at 64 starts

name: spell damage component
reason: the packet only: the combat context (attacker, damage source), the AI's attack notice (0x453F20) and the damage effect after the step are SpellLifeComponents' and the host's; Steamwoven takes no margin share from an amount of 0 or less (MG37, MagicAnomalyProfile.MarginTakesFromNoDamage)

name: spell destroy component

Ours: The viewer travel has no hide/show of the hero and followers (no off flag, no flag2 bit); the travel screen is separate.

name: follower count
reason: Original: Number of entries in a leader follower array; with the flag set the forced followers (NPC flag 0x400) are not counted; the follow limit uses the unforced count. Ours: no method of ours carries it: the count of non-forced followers is the property SessionPartyState.NonForcedFollowers (a property cannot carry the mark); Only the count without forced followers is a named member; the total is Followers.Count.

name: fatigue recovery event
reason: only the number of recovery steps, capped at 1000000 and refusing a time before the schedule

name: fatigue recovery schedule
reason: Timers (with GameSessionEvents.Delay) schedules mode 0 recovery after a positive fatigue write; the encumbrance mode (1) is scheduled in GameSessionEncumbrance; the prototype test is the caller.

name: rest heal
reason: Ours returns the whole life outcome (including waking); the fatigue write through the fatigue setter side effects (recovery timer) is the session Timers; the network packet is out of scope.

name: resting event
reason: only the number of hours, capped at 87600 and refusing a time before the schedule

name: resting schedule
reason: Timers schedules it for an NPC after positive hit-point damage (RestingDelayMs 1 hour) and never for the hero; which critters the original schedules is decided by its callers (not compared).

name: decay dead bodies event
reason: a pool's deletion at its deadline only (the session keeps the creation time instead of a queued event); a dead critter's inventory drop and deletion are not modelled

name: decay dead bodies schedule
reason: the delay only (one game day for a critter, two for another object); the prototype refusal and the event are the caller's, and only a pool uses it

name: cancel body decay event
reason: Original: Removes the pending decay-dead-bodies event (kind 24) of an object and answers whether one was removed; used before destroying a body, when a body is healed back to life and by the F11 cheat. Ours: Dead critter body decay is not modelled (only a blood pool deletes at its deadline), so nothing to cancel.

name: combat focus wipe event
reason: Original: Handler of the Combat-Focus Wipe event (kind 26): for a dead NPC with a stored killer (field 283) it clears the killer when the killer is 30 or more tiles away, else queues itself again 10 minutes later. Ours: No such event: a dead NPC killer reference is not kept, cleared or rescheduled in ours.

name: schedule combat focus wipe
reason: Original: Queues the Combat-Focus Wipe event (kind 26, 600000 game ms) of an NPC; called at its kill and by the wipe handler; refuses a missing or prototype object. Ours: Not scheduled at a kill; ours has no wipe event.

name: set concealment of a group
reason: Hero and its direct followers only (the recursive follower list is the party order); the crouch animation and art are the host.

name: set concealment of one critter
reason: Session holds one concealed bit per critter; the art change, the animation interrupt and the combat restart are not modelled; the silent no-flag outcome for missing crouch art is the host.

name: stat roll check
reason: Ours splits it: this method is only the comparison for the pickpocket perception roll; the constitution checks of critical hits are inline in CriticalEffects; the stat bounds lookup is the callers.

name: critter experience worth
reason: Original: For an NPC takes its level (stat 17) and looks it up in the xp_critter table, converting the entry to a number; 0 without an entry or for a non-NPC; used when prototypes are generated. Ours: no method of ours carries it: Only the table read exists; no code looks an NPC up by level (the worth is the stored NPC record field; generated prototypes are not built).

name: experience award
reason: only the difficulty change of the award; the PC test and the award's effects and setter stay with the session

name: sleeper into bed
reason: Original: Seats an NPC in a scenery bed with no occupant: sets the scenery occupant field (70), the sleeping critter flag 0x1000 and object flag 0x100 of the sleeper, steps the scenery frame; a sleeper on the bed tile is nudged. Ours: Beds are not modelled: no occupant link, no bed placement of a sleeping NPC.

name: sleeper out of bed
reason: Original: Takes the occupant out of a scenery bed: clears object flag 0x100, the sleeping flag and NPC flag 0x200, clears the scenery occupant and steps its frame; an occupant that does not match only logs. Ours: Beds are not modelled; the waypoint and standpoint steps, a hostile act against the sleeper or a witness and an attack on the bed do not take a sleeper out of one (SWB18).

name: summoned associate test
reason: Original: True when a PC (or the PC at the top of an NPC leader chain) has a summoned, non-familiar follower that is not an animal and is not switched off; feeds the bad-associates greeting and a script condition. Ours: The greeting slot exists (DialogGreetingStates.BadAssociates) but the host (AreaGreeting) reads it as never true; no test over the follower list.

name: can jump windows
reason: Original: Reads the art of a critter: ordinary critter art (class 2) can jump window pieces, monster art only when it is the orc kind, every other art cannot; feeds a walk flag and the window step. Ours: Ours treats any critter walker as able to jump a window piece; the art class test (no unique-NPC art, only orc monsters) is not applied.

name: set spread out
reason: The goal start belongs to the host (AI executor, 0x436960 row); the flag only is set here.

name: npc teleport map getter
reason: the write while the field is 0 (the open map becomes the teleport map) into the session's object field npc.teleport; the getter's read is QueryTeleportMap and the preparation of a change of place writes the same field (ARC-DEV-116)

name: monstrous test
reason: Inline in the combat build (flag mask over the stored critter flags); the missing-object and non-critter answers (false) are the caller.

name: encumbrance level
