name: random encounter save write
reason: Writes, into data2.sav, a count and pairs (row line id, trigger count) of every encounter table row; nothing when encounters are disabled. No random encounters in src, so no counterpart (ledger PS16).

name: random encounter save read
reason: Reads the count and pairs of (row line id, trigger count) back and matches them to the rows of the loaded tables by line id; error line on a short read. No counterpart (ledger PS16).

name: encounter terrain pair test
reason: A terrain pair (two terrain words of a world map cell) qualifies for an encounter only when both are known terrains below 19 with a nonzero entry in the table at 0x5C79C4; otherwise answers no (an out-of-range value logs an error). No counterpart (random encounters not implemented).

name: random encounter chart load
reason: Loads the world-map random encounter tables from the rules message file: counts the entries, warns when the chart is empty, parses each row (three position/radius numbers, a value read as a named list or a plain integer, then up to five monster slots) and sorts the rows by their radius field. Steamwoven reads no such tables; nearest is none (E2 of the missing-systems plan).

name: encounter monster slots parse
reason: Parses the five monster slots of an encounter table row: for each slot name it reads the prototype number and a min-max group size range, storing the prototype in the row's slot array and the range as two shorts; it stops at the first missing slot and fails if none was found. Steamwoven has no encounter tables; nearest is none.

name: random encounter roll
reason: The world-map roll for a location: skipped under the no-random switch or without loaded tables; takes the chance from the area table (default 5, times 5 while the rest window is open) and fails a 1..100 roll above it; reads the density value (default 2, zero means none), sets the night flag (before 6 or from 18 hours), refuses a town-map sector, reads the terrain value and the table override, then fires the table pick. Not in Steamwoven.

name: encounter area table lookup
reason: Walks a table of circular regions (centre, radius, value) and returns the value of the first whose distance from the given location is within the radius, else reports no match. Used for the chance, density and table-override values of the roll. Steamwoven has the distance rule (WorldTravelGeometry.Distance) but no such table or lookup.

name: encounter terrain value
reason: Reads the terrain word of a location and maps its terrain-base field (0..18) through a 19-entry table to the encounter terrain value; an out-of-range base logs an unknown-terrain error and gives zero (no encounter). Steamwoven has no counterpart; nearest is none.

name: encounter table pick
reason: Chooses the encounter table (override value, else six times the terrain value plus twice the density plus the night flag, less 8), rejects an out-of-range table, sums the weights of the rows the PC is eligible for, rolls 1..sum and walks the rows to pick one (the last eligible when the roll runs past), counts one more use of it, rolls group sizes and spawns them. No counterpart in Steamwoven.

name: encounter row eligibility
reason: A table row is eligible when the PC's level (stat 17) lies within the row's min and max level, its required global flag (if any) is set, and its use count is still below its cap (when the cap is not -1). Steamwoven has no encounter rows; nearest is none.

name: encounter table weight sum
reason: Adds up the weights of the rows of one table that pass the eligibility test; zero means no encounter can fire from that table. No counterpart in Steamwoven.

name: encounter group size roll
reason: For each of the five monster slots with a prototype, rolls a group size between the slot's min and max (a fixed size when equal), stores it and returns the total; a zero total makes the pick fail with a warning. No counterpart in Steamwoven.

name: encounter creature spawn
reason: Creates the rolled monsters around the roll location: a 1..100 roll under 51 picks one of two ring orientations; each creature is built from its prototype at a grid-offset tile, moved by the drop-tile search when the tile is blocked, destroyed if no free tile is found or another object already stands there, then turned to face the roll location and given a first action. Nothing in Steamwoven spawns encounters.

name: encounter spawn offset step
reason: Gives the tile offset of the n-th creature of an encounter group: the first goes one step along one axis, later ones step outward in rings of three (n minus 1 divided by 3 plus 1 on one axis, n modulo 3 on the other). Used only by the spawn 0x559260; no counterpart in Steamwoven.

name: random encounter hook
reason: The handler of the Random Encounters event (kind 34): re-arms the next event first (0x559640), then acts only on the outdoor map slot 1 when the PC is in no named area; takes the party location (the world-map marker while travelling) and rolls; on success closes the world map if open (removing travel, moving the party to the marker) and blocks its opener for a while, else wakes a resting party. Steamwoven has no encounter event.

name: random encounter scheduler
reason: Queues the next Random Encounters event (kind 34) with a delay of random(300, 700) minutes of game time (times 60,000 ms), via the clock's add-event call; the hook re-arms it every time, so the chain never stops. Steamwoven schedules no such event.

name: character editor open
reason: the floor only (the snapshot of the advancement sheet); the dead-hero refusal of CS2; the creation mode (CM1–CM8) is the viewer's character editor (AreaCreationEditor, ARC-UI-034); the interface modes, the animation interrupt and multiplayer are not modelled

name: character sheet close
reason: Closes the open sheet or editor: in creation mode (0) clears the PC's hit-point and fatigue damage, in modes 1 and 2 makes the interface close call, frees the window handles, clears the shown critter and snapshot globals and resumes auto-attack when its saved flag is set (any mode). Ours drops the editor floor only; no damage clear in creation mode and no interface or auto-attack handling.

name: character sheet basic info
reason: Prints the examined name (gold, shortened until it fits), unspent points, level and experience to next (a last-level text at the cap), then race, gender and age for a PC; an NPC gets race and gender only when it is not monstrous. Ours builds the view values (name, level, experience to next, points, race and gender, hidden for monsters) but not age or the layout.

name: editor stat buttons
reason: the rules of + (the − path is RefundStat); a pool stops at the caller's bound where the original has none; messages and refresh are the sheet's (S6); network clients out of scope

name: editor hint
reason: the stat cost only (the skill hint is SkillRules.MinimumKeyStat; the message lookup is the sheet's)

name: character sheet secondary stats
reason: Draws the effective levels of stats 8..15 (carry weight, damage bonus, AC adjustment, speed, heal rate, poison recovery, reaction modifier, max followers) and the five display resistances (without the magic adjustment of unidentified items), each as a number. Ours reads the same stats and resistances into the view, with effect changes of resistances not modelled.

name: character sheet stat draw
reason: The first three entries and the base columns draw nothing; maximum hit points and maximum fatigue draw plainly; a primary stat draws its effective value green when the non-innate effects raise its base value and red when they lower it. Ours carries the colour rule; positions, fonts and the hit-point and fatigue draw are the viewer's.

name: character sheet skills page
reason: Shows one of four groups of four skills (three basic groups, then tech): keeps the current group, hides all +/- buttons and shows the group's, except in the NPC mode; prints each row's training name in parentheses when trained and draws the bars. Ours builds the sixteen rows with name, training text, points and level; button visibility and group memory are the viewer's.

name: character sheet skill bars
reason: For each of the four rows draws a bar of the bar art's width times effective level over 20 (none at level 0) and computes the point cost of the next level, which is never used. Ours carries the gauge width rule as six pixels a level, clamped; the unused cost has no effect.

name: character sheet tech page
reason: Redraws the tech page: discipline buttons, the header (discipline and degree names), the effective expertise, seven degree rows (name and components) coloured white up to the stored degree, yellow for the next and grey after it, plus the + and - buttons (by degree, mode and snapshot). Ours carries the colour rule, the minus test and the expertise; layout is the viewer's.

name: character sheet spells page
reason: Redraws the spells page of the shown college: for each of five ranks the icon, the name (white for known ranks, gold for the next, grey above), the minimum-level text, and the + (below five ranks) and - (down to the floor; at the main-menu modes down to rank 0) buttons. Ours builds the five rows with known, next and locked states and minimum levels; colours, buttons and menu modes are the viewer's.

name: auto-level scheme page build
reason: Builds the character sheet's fourth page: scans scheme numbers 0..199 and keeps those whose level-name text exists (up to 200), creates the 15 row hover regions and the page art. Ours has no scheme page (the viewer panel shows a NOT READY note); the nearest method is GameSessionOwner.SetAutoLevelScheme, which only writes the number.

name: auto-level scheme page refresh
reason: Redraws the scheme page: the shown critter's current scheme name (read from its stored scheme number, or for a flagged player character from its character-file extra text) and up to 15 scheme names from the scroll offset. No counterpart in ours; the sheet never lists or names the schemes.

name: editor skill buttons
reason: the floor test only, at or below rather than equal (CP2); the dispatch and network clients are the sheet's

name: tech skill buttons handler
reason: Tech skill page button handler: hover sets the hint id; + buys a point (or sends a network packet); - compares the skill points with the editor snapshot for equality, answering nothing to refund when equal, else refunds one point. Ours: the nearest code is CharacterPointRules.AtFloor, a floor test at or below rather than equal (CP2); the dispatch, hints and network branch are the viewer's.

name: tech degree page handler
reason: Tech page button handler: hover sets hint ids (degree rows 5000 + 8 d + k, discipline tabs 4000 + d); a discipline click changes the shown discipline and redraws; + calls the degree buy and - the degree sell (no snapshot comparison, TC10); a client sends a packet. Ours has only the buy and sell rules (TechDegreeRules.DegreeLane); the click dispatch is the viewer host's.

name: spell college page handler
reason: Spell page button handler: hover ids (college tab 3000 + college, spell 2000 + spell); a tab click switches the college and redraws; + learns the next rank (spell 5 c + rank); - shows 'cannot sell back an accepted spell' when the rank equals the snapshot, else unlearns the highest. Ours has the learn/unlearn rules (SpellRankLane) and the message; the dispatch is the viewer's.

name: auto-level scheme page handler
reason: Scheme page button handler: hover over a row shows its name; a click on row k writes scheme list[offset + k] through the scheme setter (0x4A6D90), saves it to the player file in multiplayer and redraws; the up and down arrows move the scroll offset by one within count - 15. Ours has only the setter (GameSessionOwner.SetAutoLevelScheme); no page or picker.

name: alignment and aptitude draw
reason: Prints alignment (stat 19) divided by ten, truncated, and picks the alignment bar frame (value/10 + 10); prints aptitude (stat 16) on the magick side when 0 or more and on the tech side (absolute value) when negative, and places the aptitude marker at 221 - aptitude x 128 / 100. Ours computes the numbers inline in AreaCharacterSheet.Build and the viewer draws; no method carries it.

name: editor refusal message 36 raise willpower first
reason: Case 3 of the editor refusal dispatcher 0x57CEE0: with the editor open posts message 36 of the refusal texts through the text bar post 0x550750. Ours returns message 36 for a willpower key stat through the stat to message table (also used for the case of 0x55F200); the editor open gate and the post are the viewer's.

name: editor key stat refusal message
reason: When the editor is open posts the 'raise <stat> first' message for the skill's key stat: strength 32, dexterity 33, constitution 34, beauty 35, intelligence 26, perception 37, willpower 36, charisma 38, 22 for any other. Ours reproduces the stat-to-message table; the editor-open gate and the text-bar post are the host's.

name: character editor minus button dispatch
reason: Dispatches the editor's minus press by page kind (stat or pool row, basic skill, tech skill, tech degree sell, college rank unlearn) and picks the refusal message. Ours refuses at or below the editor floor where the original compares for equality only (CP4, CP6) and adds a floor to the degree sell (TC10), and picks the stat refusal message from the effective value where the original checks base minus 2 (original slip, CHW23); all owner decided.

name: random encounter map lockout start
reason: Sets the encounter flag that makes the world-map open refuse with message 602 and posts a real-time UI event (action 13, 4000 ms) that later clears it. Called by the random-encounter hook; random encounters are not implemented, so ours has no lockout (none).

name: world map open gate
reason: Toggles the window shut when open. Silent refusal without a living, conscious PC. Messages: 602 while the encounter lockout holds, 605 in a script-blocked sector or when the module load fails, 600 in combat that cannot be left (otherwise leaves combat first). Sets modes 0 then 5, interrupts the PC (priority 4), builds the window. Ours: viewer refuses in combat and off the start map; nearest AreaWorldMap constructor.

name: world map module data load
reason: Loads WorldMap.mes of the module once per open (cached name): longitude/latitude offsets from entry 20, tile columns/rows/base name/ZoomedName/MapKeyedTo from entry 50 plus the keyed map; sets the tile size, half sizes and the 320-tile snap distance. Fallback 8x8 tiles of 250 px. Ours: only the viewer art reader parses it; nearest none.

name: world map walkable state
reason: Non-scripted open: stores the town map of the PC's sector and sets walkable = current map is the keyed outdoor map and that sector has no town map. Ours: viewer decides (PcTownMapNumber); nearest none in the assemblies.

name: world map close
reason: Closing: a PC hidden by travel (field 0x13 bit 2) is shown again and may attack again, mode 0 is restored and the destroy at 0x561520 runs (notes saved, travel state 0, art freed, module cache cleared). Ours: the viewer closes; hiding and re-allowing attack are not modelled (none).

name: world map window build
reason: Finds where the party is (PC location on the start map, else the area's location; no area = error and the open fails), sets scroll limits (map width/64 - 501 and height/64 - 365, else 2000-based), loads art, buttons and markers, adds a marker for every known area, centres on the party pixel. Ours: viewer builds its own panel; nearest AreaWorldMap constructor.

name: world map off-start-map test and close
reason: Predicate: map view (kind 0) while the current map is not the start map, used for the readouts' 2000 width. The code after it (0x561520) is the window destroy: saves notes, ends travel state, removes art, clears flags. Ours: viewer closes; nearest none.

name: world map window destroy and state reset
reason: Original: with the map window up, clears hover and pointer state, runs the mode restore and ambient light restart helper, clears notes and cache, frees the per view art and video buffers and resets the map open flags and cursors; carries the ambient light restart (0x57D620) and the travel state end. Ours: the viewer closes the map and keeps ambient light updating during a journey (documented limit; same state as the rows of 0x560F40 and 0x5614F0).

name: world map tool state set
reason: Sets the tool state: entering travel stops attacking, hides the party and starts the map music; leaving it shows the party, removes WorldMap events (kind 14) and lands the party (snap, cache save). Also quill cursor, drag release snap and compass. Ours: the leaving-travel landing only; party hiding, music, attack stop and cursor not modelled.

name: world map landing change of place
reason: Saves and evicts every unlocked sector, then submits a change-of-place request to the location on the start map (flag 0x20). Ours: the cache-emptying rule for the landing caller is a rule method; building and submitting the request is the host's.

name: world map window event handler
reason: Mouse/key handler: left press adds or selects a waypoint (30 cap, known-area snap), drag and release, right release or Delete removes a waypoint and leaves travel, compass scroll, kind switches, travel button, hover readouts; a scripted-open click picks the nearest known area within 320 tiles, charges the caster, teleports (message 640 if refused). Ours: waypoint removal; the scripted teleport (ARC-MAGIC-038: the viewer's teleport mode of the world map, TerrainViewerTeleport) is built in the viewer, the compass is not.

name: known area marker add
reason: Adds an area marker (kind 5) at the area's world-map pixel with the area's name (up to 250 characters) to the view's list; called for each known area at build. Ours: viewer draws its own markers; nearest none in the assemblies.

name: world map coordinate readouts
reason: On pointer move draws two readouts: W = map width in sectors (2000 off the start map) minus (pixel x + longitude offset), and S = pixel y + latitude offset, as '%d W' and '%d S' texts into the boxes. Ours: viewer shows its own readouts; nearest none.

name: world map compass scroll
reason: With the compass pressed, a pointer outside the dead zone scrolls the view by steps toward the pointer on each axis; sets the scroll flag. Ours: viewer does its own scrolling; nearest none.

name: world map edge scroll on drag
reason: While dragging, a pointer within 23 px of a view edge scrolls the view 50 px that way (speed 10) along each axis. Ours: viewer scroll only; nearest none.

name: world map view kind switch
reason: Leaves tool states then switches among map (0), continent (1) and town map (2): town only when the PC's sector has one (else stays), continent only when a zoomed picture exists (else message 605); town switch loads the town info, walkable decides the art, redraws and refreshes the readouts. Ours: the viewer switches panels itself; nearest none.

name: town map info load
reason: Zeroes the town waypoint count, reads the town info of the PC's sector (failure clears it and the caller falls back to the map view), sets the party pixel, name, tile columns/rows and allocates the tile table, loads tile 0, sets the scroll limits and centres. Ours: the viewer reads town maps from the data itself; nearest none.

name: map marker hit test
reason: Walks the view's markers from the newest, skips those whose type is hidden, and picks the first whose picture pixel lies within a 19 x 19 box (9 px each way; about 20 picture pixels in the continent view) of the pointer. Chooses the marker whose area name or note is shown or opened. Ours: none (viewer picks by its own geometry).

name: town note add
reason: Adds a note record to the current view's list: refused when the array is missing or 199 notes are held; the record takes the next id (counter starts 200), its label flag is cleared, it is appended, the count grows and the notes redraw. Ours: Arcanum.Session GameSessionOwner.RecordTownNotes only stores and validates a whole list (cap 199, ids from 200); the add itself is the viewer's.

name: add waypoint
reason: world-map mode only; the interface record, message and redraw are the host's

name: waypoint click hit test
reason: Walks the current list from the last waypoint down and returns the first whose stored picture pixel lies within 9 px (half the marker art plus 5) of the clicked pixel; a hit selects it instead of adding a new waypoint. Ours: AreaWorldMap.Select takes an index; picking by pixel is the viewer's.

name: delete waypoint
reason: the list and its steps only (A5 under the Original setting keeps the later segments as the original does); the selection clamp is Arcanum.World.AreaWorldMap and the redraw the host's

name: travel landing
reason: the location; the teleport and the redraw are the host's

name: step area discovery
reason: Finds the area covering a location (radius test, no arrival flag); if the PC does not know it, the area becomes known, the last-discovered record is cleared when it is that area and a map marker is added; a known area only clears the last record when equal. Ours discovers in the travel step but clears the last record whenever one is set and the marker is the host's. Also called from the sector entry hook 0x564F60, which ours lacks.

name: scenery marks town map
reason: Called from the scenery description for a scenery flagged as a town map marker: when the object's sector and the PC's sector share the same town map and no note lies within 9 px, adds a question note (type 3, flags 2) named after the object at its town pixel; without a town map only a warning is logged. Ours: Session stores the notes (RecordTownNotes); the add is the viewer's.

name: travel step
reason: the clock, the discovery write, the event schedule and the redraw are the host's

name: travel position snap probe
reason: Turns the map position pixel into its sector-centre location (64 x (W - x) + 32, 64 x y + 32), then looks up the nearest known area within 320 tiles and moves to it only if the PC does not know it; the lookup returns known areas only, so that move never happens. Ours: the pixel to location part is WorldTravelGeometry.Location (0x561800); WorldJourney.Step does not run this probe.

name: sector entry area and town notes
reason: On a local PC entering a sector or after a game load: reads the sector's town map, runs the per-step area discovery (0x564A70) at the sector's location, loads that town's notes, sends the notes notice and recomputes the walkable flag; without a town map it drops the notes. Ours: none for the discovery (only travel steps discover); notes live in the session.

name: travel start check
reason: Before a travel segment starts it asks the party to interrupt its running actions at priority 3 (0x424070); if allowed it also drops the PC's maintained spells (0x457450) and answers 1, else 0 (journey refused, waypoints dropped). Ours: WorldJourney.Step has an unwired continueJourney parameter and AreaWorldMap.Start has no such check.

name: town map redraw
reason: Redraws the town map: tiles show plainly when their cell is in the town's reveal bitmap, an unrevealed cell next to a revealed one fades from black, other cells stay black, then notes, route, party and each follower marker. Ours: Session keeps the reveal bits (IsTownMapCellRevealed); the drawing and fade are the viewer's.

name: party map position location
reason: Gives the location for the world: during world-map travel the map position's location, otherwise the PC's own location; used as the position of the random encounter roll. Ours: none; random encounters and the travel position feed are not implemented.

name: text edit key
reason: only the new-character name field's typing at its end (the byte filter and the length limit) and Backspace; the cursor keys, Delete, Insert and the middle insert are not offered

name: text edit character filter
reason: Tests a typed character against the active text field's descriptor flags: bit 1 refuses the file-name characters (double quote, apostrophe, asterisk, slash, colon, less, greater, question mark, backslash, bar), bit 2 refuses letters; both clear accepts everything. Ours models only the new-character name field (flags 0), nearest CharacterNameRules.Accepts.

name: dialog start
reason: Refuses a dead or unconscious PC, an NPC that cannot speak, a second dialog of the local PC and a PC that cannot leave combat mode; otherwise ends concealment of both, leaves combat mode, turns the NPC to the PC, fills the slot, begins the reaction conversation, pushes dialog mode 3 and shows the first node or a line. Ours: only the concealment end and the host's start.

name: dialog end callback
reason: For the PC's dialog slot: clears the active word, pops dialog mode 3 for the local PC, frees the dialog state, expires the NPC bubble and calls the conversation end that clears the NPC's partner slot. Ours: the conversation-end half only; window pop and bubble are the viewer's.

name: dialog slot close
reason: Silent close of one active slot (the reset path): clears the active word, pops the modal state for the local PC, frees the dialog state and calls the conversation end. Ours: only the conversation-end half (teardown, map change); no window or bubble.

name: dialogue option processing
reason: only the voice: every processed pick stops it before the reply is processed; the reply's effects are the conversation's (ARC-SCRIPT-005), and for the pending window codes 5, 7, 8 and 9 the talk ends for the window (the NPC sheet for 5; ARC-DEV-229, NC1, WN2, F1; only the schematic window of 7 is built in the viewer)

name: generic greeting show
reason: Builds the generic greeting text of a talk request whose dialog point ran default (0x4132A0, refusing an NPC that cannot speak) and shows it through the speech display as a floating line. Ours: the text floated over the NPC; the log record, speech sound, duration and the can-speak refusal are not made.

name: float line speech callback
reason: Callback of the float line action: gives the speech display (0x568540) style 2 for a PC (type 15) and style 0 for any other object. Ours floats the text with one floater style; no PC/NPC style split, nearest none.

name: dialog script resume
reason: Runs the object's dialog script point (9) for the NPC and PC at the given line; a zero line means the slot's saved line plus one. Ours: the run (Resume with the line from the conversation's return-to-script rule); the saved-line default is the conversation's.

name: dialog reply show
reason: Shows the NPC reply text of a slot through the speech display with style -2, and for the local PC clears the dialog text and adds each option row (count at +0x464, 1000 bytes apart). Ours: the viewer builds its own reply window from the conversation.

name: speech display
reason: Shows a spoken line: in a network host sends a packet; if a listener is given and the speaker is alive and runs no animation it interrupts the speaker's runs (level 3) and turns it to face the listener; then sets the bubble text, duration and style and starts the voice (0x5688D0). Ours floats the text only; no turn, no voice start here.

name: speech display without voice
reason: Variant of the speech display: same network packet, same turn of the speaker toward the listener when alive and idle, but no voice start, and the bubble is not set when the speaker is the local PC. Ours: none (text floats; no turn).

name: dialog forced close
reason: Called when an object goes away: ends (0x5678D0, argument 0) every one of the eight dialog slots in which that object is the PC or the NPC. Ours: the viewer closes a talk itself when its partner goes; no slot walk. Nearest EndReaction.

name: dialogue voice start
reason: only the file choice (path and the female to male fallback); stopping and playing the voice are the dialogue voice player's (0x567E30 in ARC-UI-043)

name: compact life panel
reason: only each column's fill rows and the number's row (the damage percent of the 100-row column, the fatigue column capped one row lower); a zero maximum, a division by zero in the original (a crash, a technical bug), reads fully damaged and a poisoned PC's health number is centred (the original reuses the poison text's rectangle) in both modes; the window, outline, divider, colours, numbers and the hidden-interface mode it belongs to are the viewer's compact panel

name: slide show
reason: Runs the slide show (type 1 death, 2 credits, other end game): clears the queue, runs the slide script, for a death with an empty queue queues slide 0, then plays the queued slides in order over music, stopping when one returns 0. Ours: the viewer shows the death slide only; no queue, no script.

name: slide script run
reason: Runs the slide script for the show type (997 end game, 998 death, 999 credits) through the script entry at the use point; the script may queue up to 100 slides. Ours runs no slide script (the installed data has none for 998), nearest none.

name: slide picture and voice lookup
reason: Reads a slide message from slide.mes, splits it at space, tab and line feed: the first word is the picture, the second the voice path; a missing message or second word is no slide. Ours: the viewer reads the one death slide, no queue lookup.

name: follower portrait menu
reason: only the order each item sends; the menu, the target cursor and the inventory and character windows are the host's

name: follower order target pick start
reason: Starts the target pick of the walk and attack orders: pushes pick mode 18 and sets the pick filter flags, one set for walk (argument 0) and different sets for attack, switched by either Alt key being held. Ours: the viewer's own target cursor; the filters are not modelled, nearest none.

name: follower order target text
reason: After a target is picked for a portrait order (walk or attack), returns at once when the order's speaker is dead or unconscious; otherwise reads the follower menu's message for the pick kind, joins the follower's name and that text with a space and sends it through the broadcast entry. Ours: CompanionOrderRules.PortraitReceiver models only who takes the text; the pick-to-text step is the viewer's.

name: follower portraits
reason: only the red-tint test (health percent below 20); a zero maximum reads 0 % where the original divides by zero (a technical fix in both modes); the frames, their art, places and portraits are the viewer's (PA6), which does not scroll past six followers and draws no critter art for a follower without a portrait

name: portrait bar
reason: only the cropped width (none at 0 % or less, capped at 100 %, rounded down); the viewer crops the bar art by it, and the scaled draw (50 % for a follower's critter art) is not ready

name: follower portrait list refresh
reason: Rebuilds the portrait list from the direct followers array (field 241, array order, so a waiting NPC has none), grows the slot buffer, clamps the scroll offset to count minus 6 (0 when 6 or fewer), enables one portrait button per follower and redraws. Ours: the viewer's portrait panel lists followers; no assembly method carries it.

name: follower menu row states
reason: Draws the eight rows of the follower order menu: Wait is greyed when the follower is mind-controlled (flag 0x8000000 of its field 0x14), Inventory is greyed when the can-open test 0x575080 refuses, the highlighted row has its own colour. Ours: CompanionOrderRules.PortraitOrder has the mind-control rule for Wait only; the inventory refusal test (0x575080) is not read here.

name: reading window init
reason: only the five text files, each refused separately, and the newspaper filler count (0 without message 10, else the messages from 10 on, up to 999); the window's art and fonts are the viewer's

name: written item reading start
reason: only the subtype branch: the dead-reader refusal is the session's and the reading window of other subtypes is ARC-UI-049's (GameSessionOwner.UseWrittenItem, WrittenTexts)

name: reading window open
reason: Open of a written document: when the window is already open it closes instead (toggle); picks the text file by subtype (0..3 by index, 6 plaque) and silently refuses when that file is missing; pops then pushes the reading interface mode 15, stores the subtype and start line, builds the window. Ours: WrittenTexts.Read refuses a missing file; no toggle or mode push in the assemblies.

name: reading window composition
reason: the texts of each subtype: the start line and the next nine to the first missing number (the end line is never read), the markup, a telegram's headers and suffix, a newspaper's masthead, a picture's art, the prototype-14092 (the executable's 14072) background; a subtype outside 0..6 or a picture art outside 0..4095 is refused and the note and telegram buffer stops at 19,999 bytes where the original reads or writes out of bounds (both modes); the window, its rects and fonts are the viewer's

name: reading window redraw
reason: only the newspaper filler numbering (10 + start / 10, wrapping at 10 + the count of messages 10..999, a missing number stopping it); the drawing and the book pages are the viewer's

name: reading window text fit
reason: Word-wraps a string into a rectangle by pixel width and reports how many characters fit, which sets where a book page or newspaper column breaks. Ours (AreaReading.Pages) cuts a book page at about 700 characters, so the page and column breaks differ.

name: reading window markup
reason: the font (atoi), the centre mark and the dropped characters; a font outside 0..4095 reads as 0 where the original builds a garbage art id (both modes); WRD3 switch: Steamwoven reads a message without a font prefix whole (ARC-TECHNOLOGY-009)

name: reading window page fill
reason: Fills one book page rectangle through the column fill and stores the message and offset where the page starts. Ours paginates by a character count in AreaReading.Pages, not by the rectangle.

name: reading window column fill
reason: Fills a text column with the messages from the current line on, wrapped by pixel width, stopping at ten messages or a full column. Ours has no column fill; the newspaper filler columns are cut differently.

name: newspaper filler text fetch
reason: Reads the message of the given number from the newspaper file, runs the markup parse, copies the text into the caller's buffer and turns every newline into a space; returns the length. Reached through the interface callback table, caller not traced. Ours: WrittenTexts.NewspaperFiller returns marked-up messages without the newline flattening.

name: schematic window init
reason: only the two files, their order and failures, the learned count and the full list; a learned range the list cannot hold is refused (TC11, both fixed), and the fonts, art and window state are not read

name: schematic window open
reason: only the two tabs' lists: learned by stored degree, found for a PC crafter by discipline, a found number outside disciplines 0..7 left out where the original counts it past its table (TC12, both fixed); an NPC crafter's lists by its degrees with an empty found tab (NC5); the toggle, refusals, the NPC reset and the window are the viewer's (ARC-TECHNOLOGY-005/006, SW2–SW4; the viewer is outside the registry)

name: schematic window event handler
reason: Window clicks: a discipline tab sets the discipline and page 0; previous and next move one page; the other list tab swaps the learned and found lists with their saved pairs; Assemble on release shows schematic_text 1 (expertise lacking) or 0 (item missing) or runs the assembly; each hover shows its own text. Ours: SchematicAssemblyRules.RefusalMessage holds only the two refusal numbers; the rest is the viewer's.

name: schematic discipline
reason: the prototype discipline comes from a lookup the caller supplies; an empty product line or an unknown prototype gives null where the original reads an unwritten field

name: schematic record read
reason: a missing list line keeps the three zeros its missing-line text gives and drops the three values the original writes past the field (TC6 class, both fixed); the placeholder for a selection of -1 is substituted by RecordToShow

name: schematic list parse
reason: more than three tokens or a line of 2000 bytes or more is refused where the original writes out of bounds (TC6, both fixed); an empty line gives an empty list where the original leaves the field unwritten

name: schematic page draw
reason: only the button state (expertise lacking first, then a missing item) and the click messages 0 and 1 (O7, settled by a third reading); the drawing is the viewer's diagnostic window (ARC-TECHNOLOGY-005, SW5)

name: schematic component gate
reason: the search and the expertise test over the caller's view of the crafter's own items; a found item can be reserved for one component (TC4, both fixed); the slot drawing is the window's

name: schematic assembly
reason: the plan: the gate re-checked (TC5), component 1 reserved (TC4), the product alternative; the session checks the products before consuming (TC3) and consumes and creates them, for the hero or (ARC-TECHNOLOGY-006, SW7) an NPC crafter whose list gives the components and takes the products, a refused product lying on the crafter's tile (ARC-WORLD-070); no network branch

name: schematic completion callback
reason: Completion callback of an assembly: acts only when the viewer is the local PC: shows schematic_text message 2, redraws the page and plays sound 3018 plus the current discipline. Ours: SchematicAssemblyRules.CompletedSoundBase is only a constant; the viewer shows the text and plays the sound.

name: schematic text by record
reason: Reads the schematic record of a number and fetches the text from schematic_text.mes for it, returning the string. Ours: AreaCharacterSheetTexts.SchematicName and SchematicCatalog.Text read the same texts; no method carries this address.

name: schematic name by degree
reason: Schematic name of a degree: the learned schematic number (discipline, degree) then the record's name text. Ours matches for degrees 1..7; a missing record yields null where the original shows the missing-line text, and no degree range check is made in the original.

name: schematic components names
reason: Gets the learned schematic number and its record, then the display names of its two component prototypes for the character sheet's component line "[a]+[b]". Ours: no assembly method builds the line.

name: combat action point bar
reason: On the local PC's subturn draws the points left, the action's cost and the shortfall as green, orange and red shares on a 25-point scale (4.8 px a point) on the hidden-interface bar. Ours: the viewer draws a combat panel; no assembly method computes the shares.

name: combat action point lamps
reason: Given the action points A and the last check's cost P, lights up to 20 lamps in four groups of five: A minus P lamps of the left art, then min(A, P) of the cost art, then the shortfall of the third art; A of 0 lights none. Ours: the viewer's panel layout; no assembly method carries the shares.

name: combat end turn event
reason: The end-turn button and the E key released (no text focus): when the current participant is the local PC and it runs no animation, or only its goal 2 animation, starts the next subturn at once, without zeroing its action points; otherwise nothing. Ours: GameSessionCombat.EndCombatTurn zeroes the points and advances; the animation test is the viewer's.

name: fate window event handler
reason: Press of a fate button arms that fate kind (0x4F50C0) and pops the button back when refused; release undoes it (0x4F51B0) and refreshes; the Space key release closes the window. Ours: FateRules.Arm and Undo hold the rules and GameSessionFate.ArmHeroFate and UndoHeroFate commit them; the dispatch is the viewer's.

name: typed order submit
reason: On Enter in the order text entry, a non-empty text is sent as a broadcast order (0x4C2F00, the followers' text order) with the tile under the pointer, then the entry closes. Ours has only the F1-F6 presets and the portrait menu (GameSessionOwner.IssueCompanionOrder); no typed text.

name: item cursor mask
reason: the 64-bit target mask by item kind (IA3): charged or magical items take the slot-0 spell's mask, a trap device an object or a tile, an item with no spell any object; an empty slot 0 reads before the record table in the original (no installed item has one) and reads here as 0

name: item cursor begin
reason: the begin of the cursor (IA2, IA4): the refusals for a user that cannot act, the at-once apply for the masks the spell activation applies at once, the action point check, the Shift apply to the PC; the window closing, the interface mode and the cursor art are the host's

name: item cursor cancel
reason: Returns the interface to the mode below, clears the stored item and sets the cursor art global back to 21 (spell cursor). Ours: none.

name: item cursor apply
reason: the choice of the apply on an object (IA8: at once or the item-use goal 39 by the slot-0 spell's range and OIF_NO_RANGED_USE) and, in the same function, on a tile (IA9, AreaItemAiming.ApplyOnTile); the lockpick path, the run flags and the cancel are the host's

name: inventory window open
reason: The open entry: an open window closes instead (0x572340); a network client sends a request; else admission (0x572370), mode change (0x572510), partner setup (0x572640) and the window (0x5727B0). Ours: the viewer's modal window opens by its own rules (GameSessionBarter.Open covers only the barter part).

name: inventory window toggle close
reason: If the window is open, puts a held item back and closes it (the I key closes the window); answers 1 when it closed. Ours: the I key is ignored while another window owns input; no toggle.

name: inventory window admission
reason: the AREA viewer's container open (AreaContainerLoot.Open, ARC-WORLD-101) follows the loot-mode container branch: the session's open attempt (no keys), then the use script through the viewer's use-script host (skip default refuses; a native trap script is not run and the container stays shut); a container with an unlock script is not opened; the refusal text is the viewer's own (inven_ui.mes not read); the facing turn and the sight test, the critter branch's use script and the other modes are not modelled

name: inventory window mode select
reason: Returns the interface to mode 0, then selects the interface mode of the window mode (0 own: 8, 1 barter: 4, 2 and 4 loot: 10, 3: 11, 5: 0x13, 6: 0x14); refuses with 0 when holder and partner are the same object (except mode 0). Ours: none.

name: barter open stock
reason: barter mode only: the substitute container is the host's (0x45F650: no leader, within 20 tiles); every non-empty gold pile of it moves onto the NPC (0x464830 with the pile given) and, without a PC leader, both lists are marked identified (0x4643D0); a pile of 0 coins stays in the container where the original loops for ever (BT11, a technical bug fixed in both modes); the loot mode's generation of a container with flag 0x200 is GenerateContainerOnce (ARC-WORLD-100), which the AREA viewer's container open calls after the open frame and sound of a closed container (ARC-WORLD-101, LW2; the frame is recorded in the session, not drawn); the critter's sound 3007 and the steal mode are not modelled

name: inventory window setup
reason: Builds the window: stores holder, partner and mode, creates the grids and buttons, in barter mode swaps the partner for the merchant's substitute container, opens the container, arranges and identifies, closes the window if the partner sleeps, sets the restock timer. Ours: GameSessionBarter and GameSessionRestock carry parts; the window is the viewer's.

name: inventory window close
reason: the AREA viewer's container close (AreaContainerLoot.Close, ARC-WORLD-101): a container on frame 1 without flag 0x100 steps back to frame 0 with its close sound (LW3); the loot counter is the viewer's loot-window answer and the junk-pile dissolve check runs for the session's junk piles (ARC-WORLD-063); the rest of the window teardown is the viewer's

name: inventory window close for object
reason: Closes the inventory window when the given object is its holder, shown object or partner (called from the interface's object-removed hook 0x57CAF0). Ours: none.

name: held item cursor set
reason: Takes an item handle, stores it as the held item of the inventory drag with its holder and inventory location, then draws the cursor as the item's inventory art with the previous cursor over it and a hot point at (2,2). Ours keeps the held state in the viewer; nearest AreaHeldCursor.Compose draws only the image.

name: held item cursor refresh
reason: If an item is held, redraws the cursor as the item's inventory art with the prior cursor art over it and the hot point at (2,2). Left out: nothing of the held state itself, which the viewer owns; the cursor-stack calls are Godot's.

name: item lift to cursor
reason: Lifts the given item onto the cursor: puts it in the held slot, and outside network play moves it within its holder (flag 4, or 0x24 when the caller asks) before the cursor art is set to the item's inventory art with the old cursor over it. Ours: HotkeyRules.PlanItem decides a hold, the viewer lifts; AreaHeldThrow.Lift only refuses.

name: inventory window mouse handler
reason: The inventory window's mouse and button handler: press and release on grid and wear slots, right release use or move, drop and use icons, round view close, arrange, doll toggles, other party's grid and scroll, barter, steal, hover text. Ours has the own window's hit, press and release (grid move, wear, take-off, put back, icons) and the loot grid release; the rest is the viewer's.

name: barter follower step
reason: The barter window's previous or next follower button: walks the leader's follower list from the shown follower until one that passes the can-be-shown test (0x575080) is found, then closes the window and reopens it on that follower with the same mode. Ours has no stepping between followers' windows.

name: follower window eligibility test
reason: Decides whether a follower may be shown in the barter window: yes if it is already the shown one in the open window; no if it cannot speak (head test), has object flags 0x20000008 in field 0xDA, otherwise yes only when bit 0x4000 of field 0x14 is clear. Ours has no such test.

name: pick pocket plant
reason: the goal's walk to range 1 is the table's (goal 33, ARC-DEV-186; the press opens the window at sight distance); the hero's coins are not planted; the PC-only success and failure lines are the host's

name: pick pocket steal
reason: the goal's walk to range 1 is the table's (goal 33, ARC-DEV-186; the press opens the window at sight distance); the victim's item-stolen mark is not set; the PC-only success and failure lines are the host's

name: buy drop
reason: Release of a partner item on the player's grid: in barter mode (1) for a non-follower it needs the PC's coins to reach the stored unit quote, else prints the not-enough-money line, puts the item back; otherwise it moves the item to the hero. A quote of 0 cancels. Other modes just move the item. Left out: the loot take path and the grid location choice.

name: barter sale drop
reason: only the price cap at the merchant's coins; the quote, the cancel and the move are the viewer's and the session's

name: item pick callback
reason: Runs the pick: stores the held item, sets the item's no-display pick flag (0x10), computes the item art's offset from the grabbed grid cell (cell column and row times 32 in the window's layout, per mode), sets the cursor art and plays the item pickup sound. Ours: AreaInventoryDrag.Press gives the grab offset only; no pick flag or sound.

name: held item put back
reason: Puts the held item back when the drag ends without a move: for a quick slot or an item no longer in its holder it plays the sound, inserts it where it was; otherwise clears the pick flag, plays the drop sound and redraws; if its holder lost it, calls the placement helper 0x575930. Ours: Release's PutBack changes nothing in the session and has no sound.

name: held item restore
reason: Puts the held item back where it came from when it is no longer in its list: into its worn slot or quick slot, or a grid cell that fits (checked with the fit test), else the first place that passes the insert check, else drops it on the tile (0x575BE0); then clears the pick flag and plays the drop sound. Ours: no restore.

name: held item drop on tile
reason: When the held item fits nowhere, places it as a drop at the holder's tile with scatter 2 (0x466E50) and plays the item sound. Ours: nothing; the viewer never loses the item.

name: held item release if match
reason: If the given item is the held one, clears its pick flag and the held state, refreshes the cursor and redraws the window; else nothing. Used when the item is destroyed or moved elsewhere. Ours: none.

name: inventory window hit test
reason: Finds the location under a point of the window for the mode: the nine wear-slot rectangles (1000..1008) with y lowered by 41, the player's grid of 10 by 12 cells, the quick slots (2000..2009), the other party's grid with scroll in modes 2-4, and the second doll table. Ours: own-window slots, grid and icons; loot grid in AreaLootArtLayout.HitTest; no quick slots or second table.

name: item under inventory point
reason: Uses the hit test to find the item at a window point (worn, quick slot, grid of PC or other party) and its parent; an item with object flag 0x2 or pick flag 0x10 is skipped (none returned). Ours: Press looks up worn slot or grid item for the own window; the flag skips and the other party's grid with scroll are not in it.

name: bad inventory repair
reason: Repairs a holder's item list while redrawing: removes duplicate handles, then for each item whose inventory art is missing removes it, re-arranges the list and re-inserts it (insert check, pickup transfer), with warning lines. Ours has no such repair of a list.

name: bad item removal check
reason: Called for an item with bad art: if its holder is missing or differs from the expected one it logs a warning and removes it from the list (0x467860), returning 1; else 0. Ours: none.

name: inventory window redraw
reason: Redraws the inventory, barter or loot window by mode: total weight line, encumbrance level name with its bracketed carry limit, displayed damage and armour ratings, gold and four ammunition counts, item icons per grid cell, a red tint on the primary weapon below its minimum strength, the other party's grid with scroll. Ours shows weight and level without the texts, ratings, ammo lines or tint; nearest AreaInventoryArtLayout (layout only).

name: barter hover quote text
reason: Hover quote in a barter window: none in a follower's window; else the item price (0 writes a refusal phrase) compared with the partner's coins, the item script's check phrase, the price phrase; a bought flagged or worn item adds a phrase and, from Apprentice haggle, a percentage over worth. Ours shows only 'Buy/Sell NAME: N' or a short refusal; nearest TradeRules.Price.

name: identify hover quote text
reason: In the identify mode, for the hovered item: an already identified item writes the 'already identified' phrase; otherwise the quote is a fixed 100 (the price getter 0x4B1740 answers a constant) and a phrase with that price is written, then the window is redrawn. Ours has no identify window or fixed identification price; nearest none.

name: repair quote
reason: the sale price is the caller's; Steamwoven quotes from the undamaged price (TC7, a rule-mode switch); the message lines and the window's gold check are the host's

name: same-holder item move
reason: the hero's grid moves only (no other holder); the insert check's room for an item entering from outside stays the host's; the item's remove-item and insert-item events run only through a script host, and without them a move onto its own place changes nothing

name: barter transfer
reason: only the surplus the reaction change reads; the move and the payment are the session's BarterBuy and BarterSell; gambling, the rollback of a moved stack, the sound and the lines are not modelled; ARC-WORLD-090: a sold item's identified flag and the substitute container as the shown object are BarterSell's and BarterBuy's

name: take all button handler
reason: Records the shown object as the move source, copies its whole inventory list and loops it: skips an item with object flag 0x2 or item flag 0x10 (held), skips one the hero's insert check refuses, and moves each other with flag 0x21 to the hero (worn items included, no worn test); frees the list and leaves the window open. Ours has the loop only in the viewer host (QuantityBar.Ask for the stack count), no method in the world assemblies.

name: gambling check
reason: Gamble precondition for a barter item: the partner needs gambling points (skill 8), the item price must not exceed the partner's limit table value (0x4C6520) nor the hero's gold, a worn item needs partner gambling training 2 and a no-sell item training 3, otherwise a refusal phrase (indexes 2..8) is written; returns 1 when the gamble may proceed. Ours has no gambling; nearest none.

name: gambling run
reason: After the gambling check passes, runs a skill check of skill 8 (gambling, with the stored roll) between the hero, the partner and the item; on a win moves the item to the hero (flag 0x11, or 0x9 when the item flag 0x1 is set) and clears the quote. Ours has no gambling (SkillCheckRules and the stored roll exist, no barter action); nearest none.

name: skill bar button press
reason: Does nothing when the hero, or the target (if another critter), is dead or unconscious; otherwise stores the skill-use source, target and button index, closes a pending skill cursor, and applies locally through 0x57A0A0 (in multiplayer sends a request first). Ours carries the dead or unconscious refusal and the prowling toggle; left out: other buttons' skill cursor entry, the network apply test and the pending-use globals.

name: skill bar preprocess
reason: By button index: 0 toggles concealment (opposite of the hero's state, 0x45EE30); 1, 2 and 3 open the skill cursor (inventory repair window for 3) with the table's target mask; an index above 3 logs an error. Ours implements only the prowling toggle (ToggleHeroConcealment); the skill cursor entries, repair window open and spell picker follow-up are not in the world assemblies.

name: skill bar target picked start skill clear target
reason: Original: takes the skill index from the argument, starts that skill for the player on the stored target through the skill start wrapper 0x4C7050 (mask 2 shifted by the skill) and clears the stored target. Ours: only the repair start (GameSessionOwner.RepairWithSkill); the generic skill bar cursor start is absent (as the row of 0x57A1F0 says); no caller known in the export. ARC-RES-123: a byte search of the whole executable found no reference to it, so it is dead code (no rule task).

name: skill bar target confirm
reason: After a skill-bar skill got its target, refuses when the local PC or the stored performer is unconscious, else starts the skill on the target through the skill-bar start (0x57A320); in a network game a client sends a packet instead. Ours: only the repair start refuses an unconscious or dead hero; the other skills' starts and the packet are not made.

name: skill bar pick pocket start
reason: the rule only: the target's life, the stoned flag and the thief's sight are the caller's facts, and the loot of a dead target and the window are the host's; the disarm traps start (skill cursor, the 4 action points, the invocation with flag 4: GameSessionOwner.RollHeroDisarmTrap, ARC-SKILLS-1156, SP3) is built, the follower hand-over of 0x57A620 is not

name: follower skill hand-over
reason: Unless a Ctrl key is held, asks the follower picker for the best actor of the skill on this target; when it differs from the performer, builds and floats a hand-over line for the follower. Used for disarm from the skill bar. Ours has no follower substitution (nearest: none).

name: skill bar button skill
reason: buttons 0..3 only (null for another button): the original reads past its table

name: pick pocket window open
reason: Opens the inventory window on a target for the skill bar: nothing when the target is the performer; mode 3 for a PC or NPC target (object type 15 or 16), mode 2 for any other object. Ours has the start rule (PickPocketRules.Open) but the window choice is the host's; nearest: PickPocketRules.Open.

name: skill result line float
reason: Floats skill_ui line 500 (success) or 501 (failure) over the skill user, the argument choosing the line and a failure flag for the floater. Ours floats no result line for repair or pick pocket (PickPocketRules holds only the line numbers).

name: skill result line with icon
reason: Like the plain result float (500 success, 501 failure) but the text goes to the message window for the local PC or gets the object's slot icon for another user; floats it and, with the server bit set, sends it to the clients. Ours floats no such line.

name: skill result line with icon twin
reason: A twin of 0x57A7F0: lines 500 and 501, message window or slot icon, floater, and the client send when the server bit is set. Ours floats no such line.

name: skill result line float copy
reason: A second copy of the plain 500 (success) or 501 (failure) result float over the skill user. Ours floats no result line.

name: skill result line 560 float
reason: Floats skill_ui line 560 on success or 561 on failure over the skill user with a failure flag for the floater. Ours has no counterpart.

name: skill result line float third copy
reason: A third copy of the plain 500 (success) or 501 (failure) result float over the skill user. Ours floats no result line.

name: nothing to repair line float
reason: Floats skill_ui line 505 (nothing to repair) over the user as a failure floater. Ours reports the status NothingToRepair (GameSessionOwner.RepairWithSkill) but floats no text.

name: skill result line 550 float
reason: Floats skill_ui line 550 on success or 551 on failure over the skill user. Ours has no counterpart.

name: skill result line 512 float
reason: Floats skill_ui line 512 over the skill user as a failure floater, the same text every time. Ours has no counterpart.

name: skill point buy
reason: messages are the sheet's (S6)

name: skill point refund
reason: the click also stops at the editor's floor (CP6, both modes) and its length is an option (one point or until the level changes); messages are the sheet's

name: basic skill minus refusal message choice
reason: Compiler split tail of the skill refund 0x57AEB0: after a refused decrease shows the no points message when the skill has no points, otherwise the key stat message, both only while the editor is active. Messages only; the original's equality based floor and loop (CP6) differ from ours by owner decision.

name: tech skill minus refusal message choice
reason: Tail of the skill refund for tech skills: no points when the tech skill is at 0, otherwise the key stat message, only for a player in editor mode. Ours picks the same two messages from the refusal status of the press; the editor mode gate is the viewer's.

name: rest window open decision
reason: The rest hook (bed or wait): refuses for a dead PC or in a network game, closes an open window, refuses an unconscious PC (line 11), waiting where the town map does not allow it (20), combat that cannot be left (9), a bed script that refuses (8) or an occupied bed (10); else seats the sleeper, leaves combat mode and opens the window. Ours has no rest or wait.

name: rest window close
reason: Closes an open rest window: removes the pending rest events (kind 0xF), hides the window, resumes ambient lighting, takes the sleeper out of the bed when there was one and clears the rest globals. Ours has no rest.

name: rest option click
reason: A click on one of the 7 or 8 rest options: removes the pending rest events, takes the option's length from a table (hours, or the special until-morning, until-evening, until-healed values), hides the buttons, runs the followers' sleeping script event, drops the sleeper's maintained spells and queues the first rest step after 50 ms. Ours has no rest.

name: rest step
reason: Every 200 ms step jumps game time by one hour; when resting (not waiting) heals the sleeper and followers each hour; ends at the chosen hour count, at 07:00 for until-morning, at 20:00 for until-evening, while hit-point damage is left for until-healed (fatigue is not looked at), or when the sleeper is dead; the unconscious state is not tested. Ours has no rest or hourly healing.

name: rest overlay start
reason: On rest start (once): begins a screen fade-out and switches the ambient hourly light apply off while hours pass. Ours has no rest.

name: rest overlay end
reason: On rest end: switches the ambient light apply back on (it applies the current hour at once), ends the overlay effect and closes the rest window. Ours has no rest.

name: leader sleeping event
reason: Fires script event 29 (leader sleeping) at every direct follower of the sleeper when a rest starts. Ours has no rest and no such event source.

name: maintain bar save
reason: Writes the five maintain bar slots (a spell id and an active flag each) to the save file. Ours saves the bar's slots with their runs in the spells section (schema 73) rather than spell id and flag, and only for runs a save keeps.

name: maintain bar load
reason: Reads the five slots from the save and, for each slot flagged active, re-adds the spell to the bar with its icon. Ours restores the bar from the saved slots only while their runs exist (a different save form); the icons are the viewer's.

name: spell cursor no-target message
reason: the message number only (spell.mes 606); its display (0x460630) is the viewer's; Steamwoven tests the current pick's reason, the original a global any earlier area test left (MG42)

name: spell activation

name: item spell use cancel
reason: After an item's spell activation: calls 0x500570 when the cursor global 0x68350C is 0, puts the interface in mode 0 and resets the targeting globals when 0x683508 is 0, so an NPC's item use closes a player's open targeting cursor too. Ours leaves the viewer's cursor open (nearest: none).

name: item spell activation
reason: the test only; the slot read (0x4CB7A0) and the activation's call are the viewer's

name: hotkey spell activation
reason: the test only (ItemSpellPaneRules.CanActivate); the activation's call is the viewer's

name: spell cast at target

name: maintain bar add

name: maintain bar remove

name: maintain bar click

name: maintain bar hover

name: maintain bar reset
reason: Original: sets each of the five maintain slots to empty (no run, state 0), redraws them empty and sets the cached open slot count to unknown; the reset entry of the spell interface module. Ours: the empty bar is the value MaintainBar.Empty (a new session's bar and the load default), a property and no method, and the open slot count is computed from intelligence on demand (row of 0x57C4B0); no method resets a live bar.

name: maintain bar open slots
reason: the count (MG12 capped at five); the plugged art of the closed slots is the viewer's

name: editor spell learn

name: editor spell unlearn
reason: the rules of the unlearn and the refund; the spell bar update and the refresh are the host's

name: steal window hook
reason: Pick-pocket window hook: nothing for an object whose flag 0x10000 is set; a PC or NPC whose field 0xED is zero gets message 2000 in the message window; otherwise opens the inventory window in mode 2. Ours has no such refusal message (nearest: PickPocketRules.NotAllowed).

name: fatigue change refresh
reason: Fatigue bar hook: for the local PC queues a 50 ms interface event and, when the PC is no longer active, puts the held cursor item back; then redraws the hover text and the bar. Ours leaves the held item alone (nearest: none).

name: talk request default
reason: The talk callback: runs the dialog script event on the target; when it runs default, a surrendered NPC whose danger source is in the talker's party is made to flee, else the generic greeting floats. Ours runs the script and floats the greeting but never makes a surrendered NPC flee.

name: hover description show
reason: Hover hook: asks the name builder (0x57CD60) for an object's hover name and, when it answers, builds the item description (0x553BE0) and shows it in the hover window. Ours has no counterpart (nearest: none).

name: hover name by script
reason: Builds an object's hover name: nothing unless the object passes the PC test; runs the object's script with an all-zero event and, when that does not stop, builds the display name. Ours has no hover name through scripts (nearest: none).

name: player death delay
reason: Player death hook: queues the interface time event 10 for 5000 ms of real time, whose handler resets the game after the death. Ours starts its own wait in the viewer when the hero dies (nearest: none).

name: end of game trigger
reason: Slot 60 callback, called by script action 0x447220 and 0x4EFCD0: queues the interface time event 11 after 50 ms, whose handler ends the game and resets to the main menu. Ours has no end-game screen (nearest: none).

name: item spell activation callback
reason: Item use callback: nothing when the slot-0 spell has item triggers; else the activation (0x57BC70), the cast at the target when it answered 0 (0x57C110), then the cancel (0x57BFF0). Ours does the activation and the cast; the cancel is the viewer's.

name: sector enter town map
reason: Called when the local PC enters a sector (a server also for a remote one): looks up the sector's town map data and updates the town map view and its notes. Ours has no town map update (nearest: none).

name: ambient light event rearm
reason: Removes the pending ambient light events (kind 13) and queues a new one 3,600,000 ms ahead, i.e. every game hour. Ours has no hourly ambient event (nearest: none).

name: interface timed event handler
reason: Interface time event dispatcher: death (10) resets the game to the main menu when the PC is still dead, after closing the inventory and re-queuing while the menu is open; end game (11) does the same; the others refresh bars, travel and turn cues. Ours handles death in the viewer, not this chain (nearest: none).

name: ambient light enable
reason: Sets the ambient light apply flag when it was off and at once applies the current game hour to the lighting (0x57D6C0). Ours has no hourly apply (nearest: none).

name: ambient hour event
reason: Time event every game hour: applies the current game hour to the light when the ambient flag is on, then queues the next event 3,600,000 ms ahead. Ours has no hourly ambient application (nearest: none).

name: apply hour lighting and rearm hourly event
reason: Reads the game hour, applies that hour's ambient scheme, removes every other pending ambient light event (kind 13) and queues the next one 3,600,000 game ms later, so the chain runs hourly from where it started. Ours re-selects the scheme at each game hour boundary of the clock (FrameStep.HourChanged) and has no event chain, so the original updates later within the hour by the chain offset and stops during sleep and map travel where ours keeps updating (rows of 0x57D310 and 0x57D620).

name: hotkey bar save
reason: Writes the two recent actions and the ten entries to the save, each entry through 0x57DE10. Ours writes the entries and recent actions in the hotkeys section (schema 53) with kind, item and index; the item count is recomputed on load.

name: hotkey bar load
reason: Reads the two recent actions through 0x57EFA0 (which swaps their order, an original slip) and the ten entries through 0x57DEF0. Ours restores the bar as saved, checks that its items are held and refuses the whole load otherwise, and keeps the recent order.

name: hotkey bar events
reason: the left click on an entry's button only (activate, drop the held item, or nothing while a drag goes on); the recent-action buttons, the hover description (0x550150) and the key A are the viewer's

name: hotkey entry save
reason: Writes one entry: its type and slot and by type the item id and count, the skill, the spell, or the item and spell. Ours writes kind, item and index only.

name: hotkey entry load
reason: Reads one entry and by type rebuilds its object, icon and count; an item that no longer resolves empties it, an item-and-spell entry's failure fails the load. Ours validates the held item and the entry kind as a whole and does not rebuild icons.

name: hotkey slot draw
reason: the icon's place in the slot (centred or clipped); the slot art, the compact mode's fill, the count's text and the drawing are the viewer's

name: hotkey slot hit test
reason: the entry under the point; inside the band between slots and outside it are both none (the original tells them apart, 10 and 11, and acts on neither); the compact mode's band (y 563) is not modelled

name: hotkey drag start
reason: the start test only; the sources (an entry, the spell pane, the skill bar, the weapon's pane) and the dragged icon are the viewer's; an item entry's item is not put on the cursor (not ready)

name: hotkey drop
reason: the decision only (go on, end, own entry, move, put, empty); the moves are the session's (HK5); a dragged entry off the bar is emptied where the original leaves it hidden in the bar's data (HK15, a technical bug fixed in both modes); an item entry's item goes back to the grid where the original keeps it on the cursor; the drop sounds are not played

name: hotkey spell skill drop
reason: Sets the target entry from a dragged spell or skill-bar button (type and index), clears its drag flag and redraws it. Ours assigns the entry in the session; the redraw is the viewer's.

name: hotkey item place hook
reason: Hook slot 0x5E86C0: for the local PC places an item on a hotkey entry through 0x57EE30, for another holder only moves it to the entry's location. Ours has no such use-time placement (nearest: GameSessionOwner.AssignHotkey).

name: hotkey item place
reason: Puts an item on a hotkey location: an item already on the entry goes back to its holder (dropped on the owner's tile when it cannot go), then the new item moves to the entry's location and the entry is set. Ours does this in the drop, putting the old item on the first free grid place.

name: hotkey item entry set
reason: Returns any old item of the entry to its holder, then makes the entry a type-1 item entry with its icon and the held count of the prototype. Ours sets the entry in the drop; the count is queried on demand.

name: recent action set
reason: the two recent actions; the buttons' icons are the host's; the load's calls through it (HK7) are not followed: a load restores them as saved

name: hotkey key activation
reason: with the key handler's test (0x54DE50: a press, no other critter's turn, 0x566EF0 false); 0x566EF0 is the host's

name: hotkey entry clear
reason: Empties one hotkey entry and redraws it. Ours empties an entry in the session; the redraw is the viewer's.

name: hotkey recent action item removal
reason: Part of the inventory removal callback: each of the two recent actions whose object is the removed item is replaced by the default skill button of its position. Ours keeps only spell and skill recent actions (item types come only from a load, which the session refuses), so the replacement has no counterpart; nearest is GameSession.SettleHotkeys, which empties the ten entries only.

name: hotkey spell removal clear
reason: Called when a spell is removed from the book (unlearn): a recent action naming that spell is replaced by the default skill button, and every spell entry of the ten hotkeys with that spell is emptied and redrawn. Ours does not clear the bar on unlearn (nearest: GameSession.ClearHotkey, a manual drag-off).

name: hotkey bar load recovery
reason: After a load, re-resolves every item and item-and-spell entry and the recent actions by object id: a recent action whose item is gone becomes the default skill button, an entry whose item is gone is logged and emptied; skill entries get their button icon again. Ours (nearest GameSession.ImportHotkeys) refuses the whole load when an item is not held instead of emptying the entry.

name: options window page build
reason: Builds one options page: eight slots from the control table, label from message 100 x (page+1) + slot, value and enabled flag from each getter, cyclic control created and set. Ours has an own settings screen in the viewer, no counterpart in the assemblies (ledger ui-audio OP2).

name: options module apply
reason: Done on page 0 loads the chosen module and resets the interface; on failure logs a can not load module line and the window stays. Ours has no module choice (hidden by owner), nearest method none.

name: default combat mode getter
reason: Gives the options value of Default Combat Mode: 0 real time, 1 turn-based, 2 fast turn-based from the two settings; in a network game it forces both off and disables the control. Ours lists no fast turn-based and shows the stored value; nearest none.

name: default combat mode setter
reason: Writes the two settings "turn-based" and "fast turn-based" from the chosen mode (0 both off, 1 turn-based only, 2 both on); skipped in a network game. Ours has no fast turn-based mode; the turn-based setting goes through the hero switch elsewhere.

name: editor degree buy
